bank.question: When driving slowly down a residential street lined with parked cars and notice a distinct smell of sulphur or rotten eggs from your vehicle's exhaust, what is the most likely cause?
bank.explanation: A failing catalytic converter is unable to properly process all the gases from the engine, which can result in hydrogen sulphide being emitted from the exhaust, creating a smell like rotten eggs. This is a sign that the component is not working efficiently and your vehicle may be producing excessive emissions.
options: The engine oil is old and needs changing.
The catalytic converter has developed a fault.
You have overfilled the fuel tank.
The air filter has become clogged with debris.

bank.question: You see a ball bounce out into the road ahead. What should you do?
bank.explanation: If you see a ball bounce into the road, you should expect a child to follow it. Slow down immediately and be prepared to stop.
options: Slow down and prepare to stop for a child following it
Sound your horn and maintain your speed
Continue at the same speed but swerve to avoid the ball
Stop immediately and get out to move the ball

bank.question: If your engine catches fire while driving through a tunnel, you should pull over and switch off the engine. What else should you do?
bank.explanation: In the event of a fire in a tunnel, if you can't drive out, switch off the engine but leave the key in the ignition so emergency services can move the car.
options: Take the key with you for security
Lock the doors to protect your belongings
Keep the engine running to power the heater
Leave the key in the ignition

bank.question: A 'SLOW' road marking painted on the tarmac officially changes the speed limit to 20mph
bank.explanation: The 'slow' sign is an instruction to reduce speed because of an upcoming hazard, but it does not technically change the legal speed limit of the road.

bank.question: What does it mean if a road is marked with a central area of white diagonal stripes bordered by a solid white line?
bank.explanation: Hatched markings with a solid border mean you must not enter the area except in an emergency. If the border is broken, you should stay out unless it is safe and necessary.
options: You must not enter the area at all
You can use it to overtake slower traffic
You can park there for up to 10 minutes
Only motorcyclists are allowed to enter it

bank.question: On a one-way street, you may overtake?
bank.explanation: In a one-way street, you can overtake on either the left or the right side, provided it is safe to do so.
options: Only on the right-hand side
Only on the left-hand side
On either the left or the right
You are not allowed to overtake

bank.question: Why should you dip your lights when following another vehicle at night?
bank.explanation: You should dip your lights when following or meeting other vehicles to avoid dazzling the drivers. If you don't, you could cause a serious accident.
options: The vehicle ahead will see better
Your battery will last longer
So that you do not dazzle other road users
To save energy and fuel

bank.question: You are in the right-hand lane of a three-lane dual carriageway. The vehicle in front is signalling right. What should you do?
bank.explanation: On a road with three lanes, the right-hand lane is reserved for overtaking or turning right. Wait for the vehicle to complete its turn.
options: Overtake them on the left using the middle lane
Stay behind and wait for them to turn or move back
Flash your lights to show your impatience
Undertake them on the right-hand side

bank.question: In which of these circumstances are you allowed to stop on a motorway?
bank.explanation: Stopping on a motorway is prohibited except in emergencies, when told to do so by the police/signs, or if you break down. You must not stop to read a map.
options: To pick up a hitchhiker safely
If you have a genuine vehicle breakdown
To check your map or GPS for directions
To answer a phone call without using a hands-free kit

bank.question: When driving through a long, well-lit tunnel, what should you do?
bank.explanation: When driving through a tunnel, turning on your dipped headlights allows other drivers to see you more clearly in the change of light conditions.
options: Full-beam headlights
Side lights only
Dipped headlights
Fog lights

bank.question: While driving behind another vehicle at night on a dark road, which lights should you use?
bank.explanation: Dipping your headlights when you are following another vehicle prevents you from dazzling the driver through their rear-view mirror.
options: Use dipped headlights
Use full-beam headlights
Use sidelights only
Use your hazard warning lights

bank.question: Which types of vehicles are most affected by high winds on open stretches of road?
bank.explanation: High-speed winds can cause high-sided vehicles, motorcyclists, and cyclists to veer across the road; you should give them extra room.
options: Tractors and slow-moving farm machinery
Motorcyclists and high-sided vehicles
Electric cars and small hatchbacks
Emergency vehicles using sirens

bank.question: Coasting (driving in neutral or with the clutch held down) can reduce the driver's control over the vehicle, especially on downhill sections
bank.explanation: Coasting reduces your control over the vehicle because the engine is not connected to the wheels to provide engine braking.

bank.question: How can you use your vehicle's engine to help control your speed on a long, steep downhill stretch?
bank.explanation: When tackling a long downhill stretch, using a lower gear will use the engine to help control the speed of the car, preventing the brakes from overheating.
options: Applying the handbrake lightly
Selecting a higher gear and braking firmly
Switching off the engine to save fuel
Selecting a lower gear and using the brakes carefully

bank.question: What information do red circles on road signs provide?
bank.explanation: Circular signs with a red ring are prohibitive; they tell you what you must not do.
options: Give warnings of hazards ahead
Show the start of a motorway
Indicate a parking area for lorries only
Give orders and show what you must not do

bank.question: You are approaching a box junction. There is a vehicle ahead of you performing a right turn. What should you do if your exit road is not clear?
bank.explanation: Waiting for the car ahead to move avoids blocking the junction if traffic stops, ensuring routes remain clear for other road users.
options: Wait until the road ahead is clear
Sound your horn to warn the driver in front
Follow the car in front closely to bridge the gap
Switch on your hazard warning lights

bank.question: You are being overtaken. What should you do if the overtaking vehicle needs to pull in quickly in front of you?
bank.explanation: If you are being overtaken and the other driver has misjudged the gap, slow down and allow them to pull back in safely.
options: Speed up so they can't get back in
Slow down to allow them to pull in safely
Flash your headlights repeatedly
Maintain your speed and stay close to the car in front

bank.question: What does a 'SORN' refer to?
bank.explanation: A 'SORN' (Statutory Off Road Notification) is used to inform the DVLA that a vehicle is not being used on public roads. It is valid until the vehicle is taxed, sold, or scrapped.
options: A notification to the police about a car theft
A notification to the DVLA that a vehicle is not being used on the road
An insurance claim for a vehicle involved in a flood
A permit to drive a vehicle that has failed its MOT

bank.question: What does it mean when the red and amber lights are showing together at a traffic light?
bank.explanation: In the UK, amber and red showing together means you must stop but be prepared to go as the light is about to change to green.
options: The lights are about to change to red
The lights are about to change to green
You can go if the intersection is clear
You must stop immediately and turn off your engine

bank.question: You are following a cyclist at night. What should you do with your headlights?
bank.explanation: When following a cyclist at night, stay well back and keep your headlights on dipped beam to avoid dazzling them through their mirrors or directly.
options: Flash your headlights to let them know you are there
Switch to your sidelights only
Use your full-beam headlights to see the road better
Keep your headlights on dipped beam

bank.question: What driving style will cause the most harm to the environment?
bank.explanation: Frequent heavy braking and rapid acceleration cause more pollution and consume more fuel compared to smooth, progressive driving.
options: Harsh braking and accelerating
Driving at a steady speed in a high gear
Missing out intermediate gears when accelerating
Keeping your engine tuned and serviced

bank.question: How long would it typically take to fully charge an electric car using a standard 13-amp domestic plug socket?
bank.explanation: On a domestic 13-amp socket, an electric car could take 10 hours or more to charge fully. Charging points are much faster.
options: 30 minutes to 1 hour
2 to 3 hours
10 hours or more
Over 48 hours

bank.question: What does this warning sign mean?
bank.explanation: This sign warns of a staggered junction ahead. This is a type of crossroads where the side roads are slightly offset.
bank.imageAlt: Triangular warning sign showing a staggered junction ahead
options: Double bend ahead
No right turn allowed
T-junction ahead
Staggered junction ahead

bank.question: Your car gets a puncture while you are driving on the motorway. What should you do?
bank.explanation: If your car has a puncture on a motorway, try to reach the hard shoulder or an emergency refuge area and use the emergency phone.
options: Change the wheel yourself on the hard shoulder
Use the emergency telephone to call for help
Walk along the motorway to the nearest exit
Wait in the car for a police patrol to find you

bank.question: While driving along an urban street at night, you might use parked cars as a guide for your position. On a motorway, what are the white reflective studs used to indicate?
bank.explanation: White studs are the most common colour and are used to mark the divisions between lanes on the main carriageway, helping drivers maintain correct lane discipline.
options: The boundary for a temporary contraflow system
The left-hand edge of the carriageway
The right-hand edge by the central reservation
The divisions between lanes

bank.question: While driving, your engine catches fire. What should you do first?
bank.explanation: If your engine catches fire, the safest action is to pull over, call the emergency services, and keep well away from the vehicle. Do not open the bonnet.
options: Try to put it out with water from your water bottle
Open the bonnet to let the heat escape
Pull up at the side of the road and get everyone out
Drive faster to blow the flames out with the wind

bank.question: If you are dazzled by bright sunlight, you should slow down or stop if necessary
bank.explanation: If you can't see because of the sun, you should slow down or stop until it is safe to continue. High-quality sunglasses can also help.

bank.question: You have just driven through deep water. What is the first thing you should do?
bank.explanation: When deep water is encountered, you should test your brakes shortly after to ensure they have dried out and are working correctly.
options: Test your brakes at the first safe opportunity
Stop and check your tyre pressure
Switch on your hazard warning lights
Drive as fast as possible to dry the brakes

bank.question: What type of road signs are circular with a red border?
bank.explanation: Circular signs with red borders are generally 'prohibitory', telling you things you must not do.
options: Information signs
Direction signs
Warning signs
Prohibitory signs (things you mustn't do)

bank.question: Which lights should you use when driving on a motorway at night in very heavy fog?
bank.explanation: In foggy conditions, use dipped headlights. Sidelights are not bright enough to be seen, and full beams will reflect off the fog and dazzle you.
options: Full beam headlights
Dipped headlights
Sidelights only
Hazard warning lights only

bank.question: What is a potential danger if a stone hits a 'toughened glass' windscreen?
bank.explanation: Toughened glass windscreens often shatter into small pieces when hit, which can suddenly obscure your vision.
options: The glass will remain perfectly clear
The car will automatically brake
The glass may shatter and restrict your vision
The windscreen wipers will stop working

bank.question: What is a potential danger of driving too slowly?
bank.explanation: Driving slowly is not always safe; if you drive much slower than the speed of traffic, you can cause frustration and lead to other drivers making risky overtaking moves.
options: It can cause other drivers to become frustrated or take risks
It is the most fuel-efficient way to drive in all gears
It is always the safest way to travel through roadworks
It is required by law if you have a passenger in the car

bank.question: When may you drive in the right-hand lane of a dual carriageway?
bank.explanation: While you should usually keep to the left, you may use the right-hand lane if there are slow-moving vehicles parked on the left.
options: When you want to drive faster than 30 mph
When you are carrying a heavy load
If there are slow-moving or parked vehicles in the left lane
Only if you are turning right at the end of the road

bank.question: What is a sign that your car is 'aquaplaning'?
bank.explanation: If your steering starts to feel 'light' or unresponsive in heavy rain, it is likely that your tyres are lifting off the road surface on a thin film of water.
options: Heavy steering and loud engine noise
The brakes pulling to one side
The steering feeling light or unresponsive
The engine stalling frequently

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: This sign means no vehicles are allowed beyond the point where it is placed. It applies to all vehicles, not just cars or motorcycles.
bank.imageAlt: Circular red-bordered sign with a blank white centre, meaning no vehicles beyond this point
options: End of road
Warning for vehicles
No vehicles allowed
No vehicles beyond this point

bank.question: What do road signs with a blue circle generally indicate?
bank.explanation: Blue circles generally give a mandatory instruction or signpost a route for specific vehicles (like cycles or buses).
options: Mandatory instructions or specific routes
General warnings of hazards ahead
Information about tourist attractions
Prohibition of certain movements (e.g., no entry)

bank.question: Third-party insurance is the minimum legal level of cover required to drive on public roads
bank.explanation: Third-party insurance is the absolute minimum legal requirement for driving on public roads in the UK.

bank.question: You have to park your car on a road with a 40 mph speed limit at night. How should you park?
bank.explanation: If you need to leave your car on a two-way road at night, you must park in the direction of the traffic flow so that your reflectors act correctly for oncoming cars.
options: With your sidelights off
On the right-hand side of the road facing oncoming traffic
Facing any direction you choose
In the direction of the traffic flow

bank.question: Which road users are most likely to be affected by side winds while you are overtaking them?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles can create a 'bow wave' or air turbulence that can blow cyclists and motorcyclists off course. Give them extra room when passing.
options: Tractors
Electric cars
Buses with high-intensity lights
Motorcyclists and cyclists

bank.question: What does a single slanted bar on a motorway countdown marker represent?
bank.explanation: When you leave a motorway, you will see 'countdown' markers. Each bar represents 100 yards to the start of the deceleration lane.
options: 100 yards to the exit
200 yards to the exit
300 yards to the exit
50 yards to the exit

bank.question: You are parked on an urban street, waiting to collect a passenger. Why is it important to switch off your engine if you anticipate waiting for more than a minute?
bank.explanation: Leaving an engine to idle creates unnecessary air and noise pollution. Turning the engine off is more fuel-efficient and less harmful to the environment if you are stopped for more than a minute.
options: It allows the engine oil to settle, improving lubrication.
It stops the vehicle's battery from being drained.
It reduces noise and avoids creating unnecessary exhaust fumes.
It prevents the engine from overheating while stationary.

bank.question: What is a likely result of driving with worn shock absorbers?
bank.explanation: Worn shock absorbers allow the tyres to bounce more, meaning they lose contact with the road, particularly when braking, which increases stopping distances.
options: Increased braking distance
Faster acceleration
Improved steering response
Decreased fuel consumption

bank.question: You see a person at the side of the road holding a 'STOP' sign at a roadworks site. What must you do?
bank.explanation: When a worker ahead is holding a 'STOP' sign, you must obey the instruction and wait until they signal it is safe to proceed.
options: Drive on slowly if the road looks clear
Stop and wait for the signal to proceed
Flash your headlights and proceed cautiously
Turn around and find another route

bank.question: When are you allowed to use your vehicle's horn?
bank.explanation: The 'Safe' rule is to only use the horn to warn other road users of your presence. It should not be used in built-up areas between 11:30 pm and 7:00 am.
options: To show your annoyance at another driver
To signal your arrival at a friend's
To greet other road users as you pass them
To warn others of your presence

bank.question: How will your view of the road be affected if you drive too closely behind a large goods vehicle?
bank.explanation: Tailgating (driving too close) is dangerous because it reduces your reaction time and prevents you from seeing hazards further ahead.
options: The vehicle in front will be able to see you better
Your view of the road ahead will be restricted
You will be able to overtake more quickly
Your fuel consumption will be lower due to drafting

bank.question: Who has priority at a junction where a tram line crosses the road?
bank.explanation: Tram drivers cannot steer to avoid you, so you must always give them priority at junctions.
options: Cars always have priority over trams
Trams always have priority
The vehicle travelling faster has priority
Trams must stop for all other road users

bank.question: What is true about using a 'space-saver' spare tyre?
bank.explanation: A space-saver spare tyre is intended for emergency use only to get you to a garage. It usually has a speed limit (often 50 mph) clearly marked on it.
options: It should not be used for speeds over 50 mph
It can be used as a permanent replacement for a standard tyre
It provides better grip than a standard tyre
It should only be fitted to the front wheels

bank.question: Driving at high speeds can increase fuel consumption by up to 15%
bank.explanation: High-speed driving causes engines to work harder and increases aerodynamic drag, both of which significantly lower fuel efficiency.

bank.question: When is it particularly dangerous to park on the right-hand side of the road at night?
bank.explanation: Parking on the right-hand side of the road at night is dangerous because your rear reflectors will not be visible to approaching traffic.
options: On a one-way street only
Where there are no street lights
Within 10 metres of a junction
Facing against the flow of traffic

bank.question: What does this sign on the bridge mean?
bank.explanation: Clearance signs with a red circle and a measurement indicate the maximum height of vehicles allowed to pass under the bridge. 4.4m is approximately 14' 6".
bank.imageAlt: A red circle sign with '4.4m' and '14' 6"' written inside it, positioned on a bridge
options: Minimum speed permitted through the bridge
Maximum width of the vehicle allowed
The length of the tunnel ahead
Maximum height of the vehicle allowed

bank.question: How should you drive if you are dazzled by low winter sun?
bank.explanation: Lowering your speed is the safest way to deal with dazzle from low sun. Use your visor but ensure you can still see the road ahead clearly.
options: Speed up to get past the glare quickly
Slow down and use your sun visor or sunglasses
Stop immediately on the road until the sun moves
Close your eyes briefly until the glare passes

bank.question: Which type of pedestrian crossing does not have a flashing amber light phase for drivers?
bank.explanation: Puffing crossings are 'smart' and use sensors to detect if pedestrians are still on the crossing, staying red for drivers until they have cleared the road.
options: Puffin crossing
Zebra crossing
Pelican crossing
Toucan crossing

bank.question: How will your vehicle be affected by carrying a very heavy load?
bank.explanation: Heavy loads can significantly affect the stability and handling of your car, especially when turning or braking.
options: The vehicle's fuel economy will improve
The steering will feel much lighter
The brakes will become more effective
The vehicle's handling will be affected

bank.question: While checking your car, you notice a liquid leaking from a wheel. What could this indicate?
bank.explanation: A fluid leak near the wheels is likely to be brake fluid, which is a serious safety hazard. You should have it checked by a professional immediately.
options: The oil level is too high
The coolant is boiling over
The brakes may be leaking or faulty
The window wash system is blocked

bank.question: Under what circumstances may you stop on the hard shoulder of a motorway?
bank.explanation: Stopping on a motorway is illegal and dangerous unless it is an emergency, you are told to do so by a police officer, or there is a breakdown.
options: In an emergency or when told by the police
To use a mobile phone to check your route
If you feel tired and need a short break
To pick up a hitchhiker safely

bank.question: Why is it important to be cautious when following a large vehicle?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles like lorries and buses have significant blind spots to the sides and rear. Always ensure they can see you, especially when they are about to turn.
options: The driver can see everything around them from the high cab
They always have the right of way over smaller cars
They can accelerate much faster than small cars
They have large blind spots that may hide your car from view

bank.question: In which of these situations are you allowed to stop on a motorway?
bank.explanation: Stopping on a motorway is only permitted in an emergency, when told by the police, or when traffic signals indicate a stop.
options: To use a mobile phone safely
To check a map for directions
To pick up a hitchhiker
If told to do so by the police

bank.question: Signalling always gives you the right of way to change lanes on a motorway
bank.explanation: You must still check your mirrors and blind spots; a signal only warns others of your intentions, it does not give you a right of way.

bank.question: It is illegal to hold a mobile phone to check the time while you are stopped at red traffic lights
bank.explanation: Touching or holding a phone for any reason - including checking the time or a notification - is illegal while driving, even when stopped at lights.

bank.question: What does it mean if the road is marked with white diagonal stripes surrounded by a broken white line?
bank.explanation: An area of white diagonal stripes bordered by a broken white line should not be entered unless necessary and safe.
options: Do not enter the area under any circumstances
Do not enter unless it is necessary and you can see it is safe
Only use the area to overtake slow-moving traffic
Use it as a waiting area to turn right

bank.question: To whom do diamond-shaped traffic signs apply?
bank.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are specifically used to give instructions or information to tram drivers.
options: Car drivers only
Bus drivers and cyclists
Emergency vehicle drivers on duty
Tram drivers only

bank.question: When driving at night on an unlit road, what should you use when following another vehicle?
bank.explanation: You must use dipped headlights at night on all roads except where there are lit street lamps, but even then, dipped lights help others see you.
options: Full beam headlights at all times
Dipped headlights
Sidelights only
Hazard warning lights

bank.question: You see a sign for a lane marked with a car symbol and '2+'. Who is allowed to use this lane?
bank.explanation: High-occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes are designed to reduce congestion by encouraging car-sharing. They can only be used by vehicles with at least the number of people shown on the signs.
options: Vehicles carrying two or more people
Heavy goods vehicles only
Emergency vehicles only
Motorcycles and mopeds only

bank.question: On a motorway, what colour are the reflective studs between the main carriageway and slip roads or lay-bys?
bank.explanation: Green reflective studs mark the edge of the main carriageway at lay-bys and slip roads. They help show where traffic enters or leaves the main carriageway.
options: White
Red
Amber
Green

bank.question: A vehicle with a flashing green beacon indicates that it is an emergency fire service vehicle
bank.explanation: A vehicle with a flashing green beacon is used by a doctor on an emergency call. Fire, police and ambulance vehicles normally use blue flashing beacons.

bank.question: When you see a sign warning of a 'bump' in the road, what should you do?
bank.explanation: A 'bump' sign warns of an uneven road surface. You should slow down to avoid losing control or damaging your suspension.
options: Speed up to clear the area quickly
Check your tyre pressures immediately
Move to the right-hand side of the road
Reduce your speed and maintain control

bank.question: When may you use a handheld mobile phone while driving a car?
bank.explanation: Using a mobile phone while driving is a major distraction. You must pull over and stop in a safe place before using it.
options: Only while driving at low speeds in traffic
Only with a hands-free headset
Only when you have pulled over and stopped in a safe place
Only to send a text message quickly

bank.question: Why might a long vehicle move to the right before turning left at a junction?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles need more room to turn. They may move to the right before turning left to avoid the rear wheels clipping the kerb.
options: The driver is in the wrong lane
The vehicle needs more room to turn
The driver is about to pull over to the right
The vehicle is broken down

bank.question: Why is it useful to carry a dry powder fire extinguisher in your car?
bank.explanation: The main benefit of a dry powder fire extinguisher is that it can be used on most types of fires, including electrical and fuel fires.
options: They are the only type allowed in cars by law
They are cheaper than water-based extinguishers
They can be used on most types of fire, including electrical fires
They are lighter and easier to store under a seat

bank.question: What does a circular blue sign with the number 30 in white digits signify?
bank.explanation: A blue circle with the number 30 indicates a minimum speed limit. You should travel at or above this speed if it is safe to do so.
options: Maximum speed limit of 30 mph
Recommended speed limit of 30 mph
Minimum speed limit of 30 mph
The end of a 30 mph speed zone

bank.question: At what height must a child use a suitable child restraint instead of just an adult seatbelt?
bank.explanation: Standard three-point seatbelts are designed for adults. Children under 135cm (roughly 4'5") or 12 years old generally require a booster seat for safety.
options: 120 cm (3 feet 11 inches)
150 cm (4 feet 11 inches)
135 cm (4 feet 5 inches)
110 cm (3 feet 7 inches)

bank.question: In the UK, what is the general purpose of triangular road signs?
bank.explanation: Triangular signs are used to give warnings to road users about hazards ahead.
options: Orders or prohibitions
Information and directions
Warnings of hazards ahead
Tourist attractions and points of interest

bank.question: What must you do at a level crossing with twin flashing red lights?
bank.explanation: Level crossings with flashing red lights mean you must stop. You should only proceed when the lights go off.
options: Proceed with caution if no train is coming
Speed up to get across before the barriers drop
Stop only if you see a train approaching
Stop and wait behind the white line

bank.question: What do red lines at the side of the road indicate?
bank.explanation: Red routes use red lines to indicate that stopping is strictly prohibited to keep traffic flowing on busy urban routes.
options: You can stop there at any time
You may not stop at any time except in emergencies
You can park for up to 10 minutes to load or unload
Only buses and taxis are allowed to drive on these roads

bank.question: What is a common cause of accidents on motorways?
bank.explanation: Losing your concentration or 'daydreaming' is a major cause of motorway accidents. Keep your eyes moving and take regular breaks.
options: Lack of petrol stations
Turning the steering wheel too hard
Driving too fast in the left-hand lane
Losing concentration or falling asleep

bank.question: When driving on a motorway and begin to feel drowsy, what should you do?
bank.explanation: Tiredness is a major cause of motorway accidents. If you feel sleepy, leave at the next exit or services and find a safe place to rest.
options: Switch on the air conditioning
Increase your speed to finish the journey sooner
Leave at the next exit and find a safe place to rest
Drink a high-caffeine drink and keep driving

bank.question: You are following a cyclist on a narrow, winding road. What should you do when you want to overtake?
bank.explanation: When you are following a cyclist, allow them plenty of room. They may need to wobble or swerve to avoid a pothole or a drain cover.
options: Overtake as fast as possible to get out of their way
Flash your headlights to tell them to move over
Follow very closely to encourage them to speed up
Give them at least as much room as you would a car

bank.question: Your stopping distance will increase when you are driving on a road with a loose surface, such as gravel
bank.explanation: Driving on a loose surface reduces the friction between the tyres and the road, meaning it takes much longer to stop.

bank.question: Why should you avoid hanging objects from your interior rear-view mirror?
bank.explanation: Objects hanging from your internal mirror can block your view and distract you, making it harder to see hazards.
options: Improve your concentration
Help you judge your speed better
Make the car more aerodynamic
Distract your attention and block your view

bank.question: What does a circular road sign with a red border mean?
bank.explanation: A red ring on a circular sign almost always indicates a prohibition - telling you what you must NOT do.
options: Give way to other traffic
A prohibition (what you must not do)
Information about a route
A mandatory instruction

bank.question: You are at a pelican crossing. What must you do when the amber light is flashing?
bank.explanation: At a pelican crossing, the flashing amber light means you must give way to any pedestrians already on the crossing; if it is clear, you may proceed.
options: Stop and wait for the red light to show
Give way to pedestrians on the crossing
Signal the pedestrians to cross quickly
Speed up to clear the crossing before it changes

bank.question: When may you stop on a road marked with clearway signs?
bank.explanation: When clearway signs are present, you must not stop on the main carriageway for any reason except in an emergency or to comply with traffic signals.
options: To drop off a passenger
Only in an emergency or breakdown
To pick up a passenger
To check a map or GPS

bank.question: You are returning to your car which is parked on a busy urban street. Before driving, you decide to conduct a walk-around check. What is the legal minimum tread depth for the tyres on your car?
bank.explanation: For a car, the law requires a minimum tread depth of 1.6 mm across the central three-quarters of the breadth of the tread and around the entire outer circumference.
options: 2.0 mm
1.2 mm
1.6 mm
2.5 mm

bank.question: When driving down a long, steep hill, using a lower gear will help to control the vehicle's speed
bank.explanation: Engine braking helps control your speed without overusing the footbrake, which prevents the brakes from fading or failing due to heat.

bank.question: If you are driving in a busy town, what should you do when you see pedestrians on the pavement?
bank.explanation: If there are pedestrians on the pavement, especially children or elderly people, reduce your speed as they may step into the road unexpectedly.
options: Sound your horn and keep going
Flash your lights to warn them you are there
Maintain your speed but move to the middle of the road
Slow down and be prepared to stop

bank.question: What does it usually mean if you see blue smoke coming from your vehicle's exhaust?
bank.explanation: Blue smoke often indicates that the engine is burning oil, which can mean worn piston rings or valve seals.
options: The air filter is blocked
The engine is burning excessive oil
The coolant level is too low
The brakes are sticking

bank.question: If you are turning into a side road and a pedestrian has already started to cross, you have priority and they must stop for you
bank.explanation: Pedestrians already crossing the road at a side road have priority, and you should let them finish crossing before turning.

bank.question: You are following a long vehicle approaching a right-hand turn. Why might it signal right but move to the left?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles often need to swing out to the left before turning right to clear the kerb with their rear wheels.
options: The driver has forgotten to cancel the signal
The driver wants you to overtake on the right
The vehicle needs more room to turn due to its length
The driver is about to pull over to the left

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: This sign indicates a 'clearway', where no stopping is allowed at any time on the main carriageway.
bank.imageAlt: A circular blue sign with a red border and a red cross through it
options: No stopping (Clearway)
No parking on the pavement
Give way to oncoming traffic
End of motorway

bank.question: Which emergency service uses blue flashing beacons?
bank.explanation: Blue beacons are used by emergency services like police, fire, and ambulance to indicate they are attending an emergency and need priority.
options: Emergency services
Slow-moving gritters
Doctor on call
Breakdown recovery vehicles

bank.question: What do circular signs with a red circle/border generally represent?
bank.explanation: Circular signs with a red border are prohibitive. They tell you what you must NOT do or specify a limit you must not exceed.
options: Prohibitions (what you must not do)
Positive instructions (what you must do)
Information about the road ahead
Warnings of potential hazards

bank.question: What is meant by the term 'blind spot' for a driver?
bank.explanation: The 'blind spot' is the area around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors. You must perform a shoulder check to see into these areas.
options: An area not covered by your mirrors
The area directly in front of the car bonnet
An area obscured by your sun visor
The area hidden by heavy rain on the glass

bank.question: When may you use an emergency refuge area on a smart motorway?
bank.explanation: On a motorway, the emergency refuge area is only for use in an actual emergency or breakdown; do not use it for rest or phone calls.
options: To check a map
To make a non-urgent phone call
In cases of breakdown or emergency only
To have a short rest if you feel tired

bank.question: When is it legal to use a hand-held mobile phone while you are driving?
bank.explanation: Touching a mobile phone, even to use a map or music app, is illegal while driving unless it is a genuine emergency and it's unsafe to stop.
options: When you are stuck in a traffic jam
When you are stopped at a red light
When you are supervised by a qualified driver
Never, unless it is a genuine emergency and you cannot stop safely

bank.question: Your vehicle catches fire while you are driving through a tunnel. What is the best course of action if the vehicle can still be driven?
bank.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire while you are driving through a tunnel, you should try to drive it out of the tunnel to avoid smoke build-up in an enclosed space.
options: Stop immediately and run for the nearest exit
Pull over and wait for the emergency services
Reverse out of the tunnel as quickly as possible
Drive the vehicle out of the tunnel if possible

bank.question: If you are driving on an open road in very windy conditions, why should you be careful when passing a motorcyclist?
bank.explanation: In very windy weather, side gusts can blow motorcyclists and cyclists off course. Give them extra room when overtaking.
options: Overtake as quickly as possible
Stay close to them to shield them from the wind
Give them extra room when overtaking
Sound your horn to warn them of your presence

bank.question: If you are driving in a built-up area at night and the street lights are switched on, which lights should you use?
bank.explanation: Dipped headlights ensure you can see and be seen by others without dazzling them, which is essential when light levels are low.
options: Dipped headlights
Full-beam headlights
Sidelights only
Fog lights

bank.question: You are at a red traffic light. A police officer signals you to drive through. What should you do?
bank.explanation: You must stop at a red light. If a police officer signals you to proceed despite the red light, you must obey the officer's signal above the traffic lights.
options: Stop and wait for the light to turn green
Ignore the officer and follow the traffic signals
Follow the signal given by the police officer
Wait until the car behind you honks its horn

bank.question: If you are driving in heavy traffic on a wet road. If the vehicle behind is following too closely, what should you do?
bank.explanation: If you are being followed very closely, you should increase your following distance from the vehicle in front to allow more time should you need to brake, reducing the risk of a rear-end collision.
options: Speed up to get away from them
Tap your brakes repeatedly to warn them
Increase your following distance from the vehicle in front
Pull over and let them pass immediately

bank.question: You see a person carrying a white cane with a red band. What does this mean?
bank.explanation: If a person with a white cane with a red band is crossing the road, it indicates they are both deaf and blind. Give them plenty of time and space.
options: Deaf and blind
Blind only
Deaf only
Physically disabled

bank.question: You are following a learner rider on a horse. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Horses are unpredictable and easily spooked; you must pass them slowly and give them as much room as possible.
options: Drive as fast as possible to get past quickly
Sound your horn to let the rider know you are there
Flash your headlights so the rider can see you in their mirrors houses
Slow down and give them plenty of room

bank.question: How should you apply the brakes in an emergency if your vehicle has ABS?
bank.explanation: When a vehicle is fitted with an anti-lock braking system (ABS), you should apply the brake pedal firmly and steadily until the vehicle has stopped. Do not pump the brakes.
options: Pump the pedal rapidly to prevent skidding
Brake lightly and then release the pressure
Apply the handbrake simultaneously to assist stopping
Press the brake pedal firmly and hold it down

bank.question: How should you react to elderly drivers on the road?
bank.explanation: Elderly drivers may have slower reactions or failing eyesight; you should be patient and prepared for them to take longer to perform manoeuvres.
options: Honk your horn if they are slow to move off
Be patient and allow them extra time
Overtake them as soon as you see them
Drive very closely to encourage them to speed up

bank.question: Why should you look over your shoulder before moving out to overtake?
bank.explanation: Turning your head to check your 'blind spots' is essential before changing lanes to ensure there are no vehicles hidden from your mirrors.
options: To check your blind spots
Because the mirrors are small
To see if the sun is behind you
To check your indicator is working

bank.question: You are at a crossroads and intend to turn right. An oncoming driver also signals to turn right. What is the safest way to turn?
bank.explanation: When turning right at a crossroads where an oncoming driver is also turning right, the safest method is usually to pass 'offside to offside' (behind each other).
options: Pass behind the other vehicle (offside to offside)
Pass in front of the other vehicle (nearside to nearside)
Wait for the other vehicle to complete their turn first
Flash your lights to tell them to proceed first

bank.question: Why might a large long vehicle move to the left before turning right at a junction?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles need more room to turn; they may move to the left before turning right to clear the corner.
options: The driver is going to turn left instead
The driver is about to stop to unload goods
The vehicle needs more room to navigate the corner safely
The driver has forgotten to cancel the indicator

bank.question: What does a blue circle with a white border generally mean?
bank.explanation: Blue circles with a white border and symbol give mandatory instructions or indicate a specific type of route.
options: To give warnings
To give directions to parking
To indicate a prohibited turn
To give positive instructions or indicate a route for specific vehicles

bank.question: Who should you notify if your health affects your driving?
bank.explanation: You must tell the DVLA if your health might affect your ability to drive safely. This includes certain eye conditions, heart problems, or neurological issues.
options: The DVLA
Your insurance company only
The local police station
The Department for Transport

bank.question: What information may be found on a small plate beneath a triangular warning sign?
bank.explanation: Underneath these signs, there may be a distance or a direction arrow indicating how long or where the restriction applies.
options: The speed limit for the area
The distance to the nearest car park
The distance or time for which a restriction applies
The telephone number for traffic reports

bank.question: You are entering a well-lit tunnel in motorway traffic. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Tunnels can be dangerous due to sudden changes in light and the confined space. Dipped headlights help you see and be seen without dazzling others via mirrors.
options: Full-beam headlights
Side lights only
Dipped headlights
Fog lights

bank.question: What is meant by the term 'engine braking'?
bank.explanation: Using the gears to help the vehicle slow down rather than relying solely on the brakes is known as engine braking. This helps prevent brake fade on long downhill stretches.
options: Braking earlier than necessary
Using the handbrake to assist the footbrake
Changing to a lower gear when travelling downhill
Driving with the clutch pedal held down

bank.question: What is one of the main risks of having over-inflated tyres?
bank.explanation: Over-inflated tyres have a smaller contact patch with the road surface, which reduces the amount of grip available for steering and braking.
options: Increase the comfort of the ride
Reduce the wear on the centre of the tread
Decrease the amount of grip on the road
Improve the suspension's performance

bank.question: What does a circular road sign with a red border and a red cross on a blue background mean?
bank.explanation: Clearway signs (a red cross on a blue circle) indicate that you must not stop at any time, even to pick up or set down passengers.
options: No parking during daytime hours
No stopping at any time
No entry for motor vehicles
National speed limit applies

bank.question: The legal minimum depth of tread for car tyres is 1.0mm
bank.explanation: The legal minimum tread depth for car tyres is 1.6 mm across the central three-quarters of the tread and around the whole circumference.

bank.question: If you have to park your car facing uphill, which way should you turn your steering wheel?
bank.explanation: When parking uphill, turning the wheels away from the kerb (and selecting a gear or 'Park') ensures the car rolls into the kerb rather than into the road.
options: Towards the kerb
Parallel to the kerb
Away from the kerb
It doesn't matter as long as the handbrake is on

bank.question: If you are a new driver, your licence will be revoked if you get how many penalty points within two years of passing?
bank.explanation: Under the New Drivers Act, your licence is revoked if you get 6 or more points within 2 years of passing your first practical test.
options: 3 points
12 points
6 points
9 points

bank.question: You are required to use your full-beam headlights when driving on any road that has street lighting
bank.explanation: Sidelights must be used between sunset and sunrise, but you must use headlights at night on all roads without street lighting or where the speed limit exceeds 30 mph.

bank.question: When is a vehicle most likely to use the most fuel?
bank.explanation: A vehicle is likely to use more fuel when the engine is cold because it runs less efficiently. Short journeys are particularly heavy on fuel consumption.
options: When the engine is at its normal operating temperature
When the engine is cold
When you are driving in a high gear
When the car has been recently serviced

bank.question: What is likely to happen if you drive too fast in heavy rain? (Aquaplaning)?
bank.explanation: In heavy rain, tyres can lose contact with the road surface due to a layer of water building up. This is known as aquaplaning.
options: The brakes will overheat and fade
The steering will become very heavy
The engine will cut out suddenly
The tyres will lose their grip on the road

bank.question: Which type of road user is most affected by strong side winds?
bank.explanation: In windy conditions, cyclists, motorcyclists, and high-sided vehicles can be blown sideways. Always allow extra room when overtaking them.
options: Tractors towing heavy loads
Cyclists and motorcyclists
Sports cars with low ground clearance
Estate cars carrying roof boxes

bank.question: What does a 'clearway' sign mean?
bank.explanation: On a clearway, you must not stop at any time unless there is an emergency or you are told to by a police officer.
options: No overtaking at any time
No stopping at any time
No parking between 8 am and 6 pm
No turning right into side roads

bank.question: A vehicle with a flashing blue beacon indicates it is an emergency vehicle
bank.explanation: Blue beacons are used by emergency vehicles such as police, fire, or ambulance services to indicate they are responding to an emergency.

bank.question: What is one of the main risks of driving with tyres that are worn below the legal limit?
bank.explanation: Worn tyres are dangerous because they have less grip, increasing the risk of skidding and aquaplaning. The legal minimum tread depth is 1.6mm.
options: Increased fuel consumption
The braking system will become more sensitive
Increased risk of skidding in wet weather missions
The steering will become much lighter

bank.question: You miss your exit on a motorway. What should you do?
bank.explanation: If you miss your exit, you must continue to the next junction. Never reverse or try to cross the central reservation.
options: Reverse back to the exit on the hard shoulder
Do a U-turn through the central reservation gap
Stop and wait for the traffic to clear so you can reverse
Carry on to the next exit

bank.question: When parking at night, when MUST you leave your sidelights on?
bank.explanation: Leaving your sidelights on when parked on a road with a speed limit over 30mph helps other drivers see your vehicle in the dark.
options: On a road with a 20 mph limit
When parked in a designated lay-by
On a road with a 30 mph limit
On a road with a speed limit greater than 30 mph

bank.question: When driving on a motorway and begin to feel sleepy, what should you do?
bank.explanation: If you feel drowsy while driving on a motorway, the safest course of action is to leave at the next exit or services and find a safe place to rest.
options: Speed up to get home faster
Open the window and turn on the radio loudly
Stop on the hard shoulder for a nap
Leave the motorway at the next exit or services

bank.question: If you gain six or more penalty points within two years of passing your first driving test, your licence will be revoked
bank.explanation: Under the 'New Drivers Act', your licence will be revoked if you get 6 or more points within 2 years of passing your first practical driving test.

bank.question: A police officer is directing traffic and signals for you to stop. What must you do?
bank.explanation: You must always obey the instructions of a police officer, even if they contradict traffic lights or signs, as they may be managing an incident.
options: Stop immediately, even if it blocks a junction
Continue driving until you reach a traffic light
Ignore the signal if you think it is safe to do so
Wait for a traffic sign to confirm the signal

bank.question: You are inspecting your tyres while parked on a residential street. What is the legal minimum tread depth for a car tyre across the central three-quarters of its width?
bank.explanation: UK law requires car tyres to have a minimum tread depth of 1.6 mm across the central 75% of the tread and around the entyre circumference. Insufficient tread depth is dangerous, especially in wet weather, and can lead to fines and penalty points.
options: 1.0 mm
2.5 mm
1.6 mm
2.0 mm

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: A red circle with a car and a motorcycle means no motor vehicles are allowed. This is often used for pedestrian zones or quiet lanes.
bank.imageAlt: A circular sign with a red border containing a car and a motorcycle
options: Motorcycles only are allowed
Warning: motor vehicles ahead
No motor vehicles allowed
No cars or motorcycles on weekends

bank.question: What do green reflective studs indicate on a motorway?
bank.explanation: Green studs are used to mark the edge of the main carriageway where it crosses a slip road or a lay-by.
options: The left-hand edge of the motorway
The central reservation boundary
The slip road entrance or exit
The hard shoulder boundaries

bank.question: You are carrying a bulky load on your roof rack. What is the maximum distance it can overhang the rear of your car before it must be marked?
bank.explanation: Any load that overhangs more than 2 metres at the rear must be marked with red and white 'long load' marker boards.
options: 20 centimetres
50 centimetres
1 metre
2 metres

bank.question: Why should you be extra cautious when sharing the road with trams?
bank.explanation: Trams cannot steer to avoid you because they run on fixed rails. They are also very quiet and move surprisingly fast.
options: They cannot steer to avoid you
They always have the right of way at all junctions
They travel at much higher speeds than cars
They stop much faster than other vehicles

bank.question: You are following a long vehicle approaching a left-hand turn. What should you do?
bank.explanation: When you see a 'long vehicle' sign on a lorry or bus, remember they need more room to turn. They may move to the right before turning left to clear the kerb.
options: Pull up closely behind it to stay in its mirrors
Overtake it on the left if there is space
Stay well back as it may need to use more of the road to turn
Sound your horn to let the driver know you are there

bank.question: What will happen if your car wheels are out of balance?
bank.explanation: Unbalanced wheels cause the steering wheel to vibrate at certain speeds, which can lead to premature wear of steering and suspension.
options: The steering will vibrate
The brakes will pull to one side
The engine will overheat
The tyres will squeal on corners

bank.question: How can you reduce the glare from the sun when it is low in the sky?
bank.explanation: Low sun, especially in winter, can be very dazzling. Using your sun visor and wearing sunglasses can help maintain clear vision.
options: Brake hard to reduce your speed quickly
Close your eyes for a second to let them adjust
Use your sun visor and wear sunglasses if possible
Pull over and wait for the sun to set before moving

bank.question: Coasting (travelling in neutral or with the clutch pressed down) is a recommended technique for saving fuel when driving downhill
bank.explanation: Coasting (driving in neutral or with the clutch down) reduces control because engine braking is eliminated and steering becomes less effective.

bank.question: If you are driving on a narrow urban street and see a rectangular blue sign with a graphic of a car, showing two wheels on the pavement and two on the road, what does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: This sign indicates that you are permitted to park partially on the pavement. This is often used on narrow roads to help keep the carriageway clear and allow traffic to pass.
options: You may park partially on the verge or pavement.
End of all parking restrictions.
Parking on the pavement is strictly prohibited.
Parking is for permit holders only.

bank.question: When are you allowed to drive through a red traffic light?
bank.explanation: You must stop at a red light unless a police officer or traffic warden signals you to proceed. Obstruction or empty roads don't change the law.
options: The road is clear and there are no pedestrians around
You are turning left into a minor road
You are driving a high-performance vehicle
When directed to do so by a police officer

bank.question: While driving down a quiet residential street, you consider the emissions from your vehicle. What is the primary function of your car's catalytic converter?
bank.explanation: The catalytic converter is a vital part of the exhaust system that changes toxic substances into less harmful ones, such as carbon dioxide and water vapour. It is a legal requirement and essential for passing an MOT emissions test.
options: To monitor oxygen levels for optimal fuel consumption.
To convert hazardous exhaust pollutants into less harmful gases.
To trap diesel particulates and prevent black smoke.
To minimise engine volume and reduce noise pollution.

bank.question: When is it appropriate to use your car's horn?
bank.explanation: You should only use your horn to warn other road users of your presence. It should not be used to greet people, express anger, or in built-up areas between 11:30 pm and 7:00 am unless there is danger.
options: To greet friends in other cars
To signal your annoyance at a slow driver
To warn others of your presence
To signal that you have right of way at a junction

bank.question: What does a 'High-occupancy vehicle' (HOV) lane mean?
bank.explanation: High-occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes are reserved for vehicles with a certain number of occupants (usually 2 or more) to encourage car-pooling.
options: Only vehicles carrying heavy loads can use this lane
Only emergency vehicles are permitted in this lane
Vehicles must have at least the minimum number of people specified on the sign
The lane is only for vehicles travelling at high speeds

bank.question: You need to check your engine oil level and have parked on a street with a pronounced camber. Why is it essential to move the vehicle onto level ground before performing the check?
bank.explanation: The vehicle must be on a level surface to ensure the oil in the sump is not tilted. A sloped surface will lead to an inaccurate measurement on the dipstick, which could cause you to either underfill or overfill the engine.
options: To allow the oil pressure to stabilise.
To prevent the bonnet from locking unexpectedly.
To ensure the dipstick reading is accurate.
To stop oil from spilling into the engine bay.

bank.question: When driving along a narrow country lane with high hedges that are limiting your view ahead, what is the most effective way to anticipate oncoming hazards?
bank.explanation: When your view is restricted, you should look for other clues. Oncoming vehicle lights can often be seen as reflections in windows, on wet roads, or against trees and hedges before you can see the vehicle itself, giving you early warning.
options: Position your vehicle in the middle of the road to claim your space.
Watch for the reflection of approaching headlights in windows or on wet road surfaces.
Focus entyrely on the road surface immediately in front of your car.
Accelerate to clear the blind areas more quickly.

bank.question: You have missed your motorway exit. What should you do next?
bank.explanation: If you miss your exit, continue to the next junction. Never reverse or attempt a U-turn on a motorway.
options: Carry on to the next junction
Stop and wait for a gap in traffic to reverse
Reverse back along the hard shoulder
Do a U-turn at the next emergency central reservation gap

bank.question: You are entering a contraflow system on a motorway. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Contraflow systems mean you are travelling close to oncoming traffic in narrow lanes. You should reduce speed and keep a safe distance.
options: Increase your speed to clear it quickly
Switch lanes frequently to find the fastest flow
Reduce your speed and keep a safe distance following the signs
Switch your headlights to full beam to be seen

bank.question: What do circular signs with blue backgrounds generally provide?
bank.explanation: Blue circles with white symbols generally give a mandatory instruction, such as 'Turn Left Ahead' or 'Keep Left'.
options: Warnings of hazards ahead
Prohibitions (things you must not do)
Information about tourist attractions
Mandatory instructions (things you must do)

bank.question: You are following a large vehicle. Why should you stay well back from it?
bank.explanation: When following a large vehicle, staying well back allows the driver to see you in their mirrors and gives you a better view of the road ahead.
options: Moving closer so you can see past it better
Staying well back so the driver can see you in their mirrors
Flashing your headlights to let them know you are there
Overtaking as quickly as possible on the left-hand side

bank.question: What does a long white line with short gaps in the middle of the road signify?
bank.explanation: A long white line with short gaps (hazard warning line) means there is a hazard ahead, such as a bend or a junction.
options: You are entering a high-speed zone
There is a hazard ahead
You are on a one-way street
Overtaking is strictly prohibited

bank.question: The purpose of a car's 'crumple zone' is to absorb the energy from a collision
bank.explanation: Modern cars have a 'safety' or 'crumple' zone designed to absorb the energy of an impact, protecting the occupants in the cabin.

bank.question: You see an ambulance with blue flashing lights behind you. What should you do?
bank.explanation: If you are being followed by an ambulance with blue flashing lights, you should pull over as soon as it is safe to do so to let it pass.
options: Maintain your speed and stay in the middle of the road
Speed up to get out of its way quickly
Pull over when it is safe to do so to let it pass
Brake harshly immediately to stop recorded progress

bank.question: You are joining a motorway from a slip road that is very short. What should you do?
bank.explanation: When the slip road is short, you must wait for a safe gap in the motorway traffic. Do not force your way in or drive onto the hard shoulder.
options: Force your way into the left-hand lane
Drive along the hard shoulder until you find a gap
Stop and wait for a safe gap in the traffic
Speed up and overtake the cars in the left-hand lane

bank.question: What is 'engine braking'?
bank.explanation: By easing off the accelerator before you need to brake, you use the engine to slow the car down, saving fuel and reducing brake wear.
options: Using the engine to slow the car by easing off the accelerator early
Coating the gears in special oil to reduce friction
Driving in a high gear with the accelerator fully pressed
Switching the engine off while going down long hills

bank.question: What do these signs mean?
bank.explanation: These yellow diversion signs use symbols such as a square, circle, triangle or diamond to guide drivers along a temporary diversion route around roadworks or a closure.
bank.imageAlt: Yellow diversion route signs with black route symbols
options: Only cars and motorcycles allowed
Roadworks ahead
Diversion routes
Ring roads ahead

bank.question: Belisha beacons are the flashing yellow lights used at Zebra crossings
bank.explanation: Zebra crossings have flashing yellow beacons (Belisha beacons) on both sides of the road to alert drivers to the crossing.

bank.question: Your vehicle requires an MOT test, which it passes on 15th May. By what date must the next MOT be conducted?
bank.explanation: An MOT certificate is valid for 12 months. The expiry date is one year minus one day from the date of the test.
options: 14th May of the next year
15th November of the same year
14th May two years later
15th May of the next year

bank.question: Rumble strips are often used to alert drivers to a hazard ahead, such as a roundabout or a sharp bend
bank.explanation: Rumble strips or raised road markings are often used on the approach to hazards such as roundabouts or dangerous bends to encourage drivers to slow down.

bank.question: Why might a long vehicle signal left but move out to the right before turning into a narrow side road?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles often need more room to turn; they may move to the right initially to successfully navigate a tight left-hand turn.
options: The driver is in the wrong lane and will soon correct it
The driver is preparing to turn right instead
The vehicle needs more room to turn because of its length
The driver is signalling for you to overtake on the left

bank.question: What does a circular sign with a red border containing a bicycle image mean?
bank.explanation: A circular sign with a red border and a bicycle inside means 'no cycling'. Circles almost always give orders.
options: Cycling is encouraged here
No cycling allowed
A cycle route lies ahead
Watch out for children on bikes

bank.question: You see a horse rider in the left-hand lane approaching a roundabout. What should you expect them to do?
bank.explanation: Equestrians often take the left-hand lane even when turning right at a roundabout to stay away from faster traffic. Stay well back and give them plenty of room.
options: Wait for them to move into the right-hand lane before they turn
Sound your horn to tell them they are in the wrong lane
Stay well back and give them plenty of room
Overtake them on the right as quickly as possible

bank.question: What do double yellow lines painted on the kerb mean?
bank.explanation: Yellow lines on the kerb indicate waiting restrictions. Two lines mean 'no loading or unloading at any time'.
options: No loading or unloading at any time
No parking during daylight hours
Loading is permitted for 20 minutes only
A bus stop is nearby

bank.question: When may a Blue Badge holder park on double yellow lines?
bank.explanation: Blue Badge holders may park on single or double yellow lines for up to 3 hours, provided they do not cause an obstruction and there are no loading restrictions.
options: At any time without a time limit
Only if there are no other spaces available in the street
For up to three hours if no obstruction is caused
Only if they are accompanied by an able-bodied person

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: A 'No Entry' sign is a red circle with a white horizontal bar. It means you must not enter that road.
bank.imageAlt: A red circular sign with a white horizontal bar
options: No parking
No waiting
No entry
No through road

bank.question: How does a correctly adjusted head restraint help in a crash?
bank.explanation: A correctly adjusted head restraint will reduce the risk of neck injury (whiplash) if your vehicle is hit from behind.
options: It helps to prevent neck injury in a collision
It makes the driver feel more comfortable on long journeys
It is a legal requirement for the driver to rest their head on it
It helps the driver to maintain a better posture

bank.question: A Statutory Off-Road Notification (SORN) must be renewed every 12 months, even if the vehicle remains off the road
bank.explanation: A SORN remains valid until the vehicle is re-taxed, sold, scrapped, or exported; it does not need to be renewed annually.

bank.question: How is total stopping distance calculated?
bank.explanation: The 'Thinking Distance' plus the 'Braking Distance' equals the total 'Stopping Distance' of your vehicle.
options: Braking distance minus thinking distance
Thinking distance multiplied by speed
Reaction time plus acceleration time
Thinking distance plus braking distance

bank.question: On a motorway at night, what colour reflective studs mark the right-hand edge of the carriageway beside the central reservation?
bank.explanation: Amber reflective studs are used on motorways to denote the right-hand edge of the carriageway, separating it from the central reservation.
options: Green
Red
Amber
White

bank.question: You are the first person to arrive at the scene of an accident. What is the first thing you should do?
bank.explanation: The first thing you should do after an accident is check the area for further danger, such as oncoming traffic or fire.
options: Check for further danger
Call your insurance company
Move the injured people out of the cars immediately
Take photos for social media

bank.question: You need to change your destination on your sat nav while driving. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Touching a mobile phone, even to use a map, is illegal while driving. You should set your route before starting the journey.
options: Pull up in a safe, legal place before adjusting it
Wait until you reach a red traffic light
Ask a pedestrian for help at the next junction
Slow down and adjust it quickly while moving

bank.question: When driving and a warning light for your brakes stays on, what does this likely indicate?
bank.explanation: In many modern cars, the brake fluid level is monitored by a sensor that illuminates a warning light on the dashboard if it drops too low.
options: The engine oil level is low
The handbrake is partially engaged while moving
The air conditioning system has a fault
The brake fluid level may be low

bank.question: When driving on a road that has been dry for a long time. It starts to rain, why should you be extra cautious?
bank.explanation: A long period of dry weather causes oil and rubber to build up on the road surface. When it first rains, this creates a very slippery layer.
options: Predict that the road surface will be very slippery
Drive at the normal speed limit as the rain clears the dust
Assume that grip will be better than on a totally dry road
Only use your fog lights if it is daytime

bank.question: A train has just passed at a level crossing but the red lights are still flashing. What should you do?
bank.explanation: If you reach a railway level crossing and the red lights continue to flash after a train has passed, stay stopped. Another train may be coming from the other direction.
options: Drive across quickly before the barriers come down again
Wait for 30 seconds and then proceed with caution
Stay where you are and continue to wait
Get out of the car to see if the track is clear

bank.question: What is a key feature of 'eco-safe' driving?
bank.explanation: Eco-safe driving includes looking well ahead so you can adjust your speed smoothly, avoiding unnecessary braking and acceleration.
options: Using your hazard lights in heavy traffic
Planning ahead to avoid unnecessary braking
Always driving in a low gear to maintain control
Revving the engine while waiting at traffic lights

bank.question: When may you use hazard warning lights while the vehicle is moving?
bank.explanation: Hazard warning lights should be used on motorways or unrestricted dual carriageways to warn following traffic that there is an obstruction or slow-moving traffic ahead.
options: To warn following traffic of a hazard or obstruction ahead
To thank another driver for letting you out
To signal that you are parking on double yellow lines
To warn other drivers that you are driving slowly in fog

bank.question: Reflective road studs (cats' eyes) are designed to provide extra illumination for your headlights in rural areas
bank.explanation: Reflective road studs are not lights. They reflect your headlights and help show the road layout, lane edges and carriageway boundaries in poor visibility or darkness.

bank.question: How should you respond after accidentally missing a motorway exit?
bank.explanation: If you miss your exit, never reverse or attempt a U-turn on a motorway. Drive to the next junction and find a safe way to return.
options: Carry on to the next junction
Reverse back to the junction on the hard shoulder
Make a U-turn at the next gap in the central reservation
Stop and wait for a police escort

bank.question: Driving in neutral for long distances ('coasting') is a recommended technique to save fuel and increase vehicle control
bank.explanation: Coasting (driving in neutral or with the clutch down) reduces your control over the car, particularly during cornering and braking.

bank.question: What is likely to happen if you use your brakes continuously on a long, steep descent?
bank.explanation: Excessive use of the brake pedal on long downhill sections can cause the brakes to overheat and lose their effectiveness.
options: The brakes will overheat and become less effective
The fuel consumption will increase significantly
The suspension will become damaged
The gearbox will lock into the current gear

bank.question: What can unbalanced wheels on your vehicle cause?
bank.explanation: Unbalanced wheels cause the steering wheel to vibrate at certain speeds. This should be fixed by a garage to prevent damage to suspension and tyres.
options: The brakes to fail
The car to pull to one side
The steering to vibrate
The tyres to deflate

bank.question: You have accidentally driven past your intended exit on a motorway. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Missing a turn on a motorway is common; you must never reverse or stop. Drive to the next exit and find a safe way back.
options: Continue to the next exit and find a route back
Reverse back along the hard shoulder to the exit
Perform a U-turn across the central reservation
Stop and wait for a gap in traffic to reverse

bank.question: When driving in a busy town, what does a white arrow painted on the road pointing towards the left kerb usually mean if accompanied by a dashed line?
bank.explanation: A white arrow pointing left with 'BUS LANE' markings usually indicates where the bus lane ends or where you may cross it to turn left.
options: The bus lane is coming to an end
Only buses are allowed to turn left here
You must enter the bus lane immediately
Buses must yield to your vehicle here

bank.question: If you are driving in heavy rain and the steering suddenly feels very light, what should you do?
bank.explanation: If your steering suddenly feels light and unresponsive in heavy rain, your tyres may be 'aquaplaning' on a film of water. Ease off the accelerator to slow down.
options: Apply the handbrake firmly but briefly
Ease off the accelerator and do not brake
Brake hard to clear the water from the tyres
Steer sharply from side to side to regain grip

bank.question: How should you use the lanes on a clear, three-lane dual carriageway?
bank.explanation: On a multi-lane dual carriageway, you should always stay in the left-hand lane unless you are overtaking slower-moving traffic.
options: Stay in whichever lane has the least traffic
Drive in the right-hand lane to stay out of the way of lorries
Use the left-hand lane unless you are overtaking
Drive in the middle of the two lanes to stay safe

bank.question: Using a lower gear when driving down a long, steep hill can help prevent your brakes from overheating
bank.explanation: Using the engine to slow down (engine braking) on a long downhill slope helps prevent the brakes from overheating and becoming less effective.

bank.question: At a Pelican crossing, you must stay stopped when the amber light is flashing, even if the crossing is completely clear
bank.explanation: You must stop at a Pelican crossing if the amber light is flashing and a pedestrian is still on the crossing. If the crossing is clear, you may proceed.

bank.question: You are parking on a road at night that has a speed limit of 40 mph. What lights must you leave on?
bank.explanation: If you are parking on a road at night with a speed limit over 30 mph, you must leave your sidelights (parking lights) on so other drivers can see you.
options: Dipped headlights
Full beam headlights
Hazard warning lights
Sidelights

bank.question: Why is 'tailgating' (following a vehicle too closely) dangerous?
bank.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous because it significantly reduces your reaction time and field of vision if the car in front stops suddenly.
options: It reduces your field of vision and reaction time
It helps you stay in the slipstream and save fuel
It encourages the driver in front to speed up
It is the best way to signal you want to overtake

bank.question: For how long is an MOT certificate usually valid?
bank.explanation: An MOT certificate for a car over three years old is valid for exactly one year from the date of issue.
options: One year
Two years
Three years
Until the vehicle is sold

bank.question: How should you dispose of a used vehicle battery?
bank.explanation: Standard alkaline batteries should be recycled at local collection points, while car batteries must be taken to a garage or local authority site.
options: Put it in the household rubbish bin
Leave it on the pavement for collection
Burn it in a controlled environment
Take it to a local authority site or a garage

bank.question: What can be a result of driving with under-inflated tyres?
bank.explanation: Under-inflated tyres increase rolling resistance, which makes the engine work harder and burns more fuel. They also affect steering and braking.
options: Increased engine temperature
Reduced wind resistance
Lower insurance premiums
Increased fuel consumption

bank.question: Why should you be particularly cautious of trams?
bank.explanation: Trams are powered by electricity and run on fixed rails, making them very quiet. They cannot steer out of your way.
options: They cannot stop quickly
They move quietly and cannot steer to avoid you
They always have priority over emergency vehicles
They emit heavy exhaust fumes

bank.question: A long, heavy vehicle ahead is signalling left but moving out to the right before turning. What should you do?
bank.explanation: A long vehicle may need to swing out to the right before turning left. Stay well back and do not try to overtake on either side, because the vehicle may cut across your path as it turns.
options: Overtake on the left as they move right
Overtake on the right as they slow down
Sound your horn to warn them they are in the wrong lane
Stay well back and give them plenty of room

bank.question: How should you behave when driving in slow-moving motorway traffic?
bank.explanation: In slow-moving traffic on a motorway, do not change lanes unnecessarily as this increases the risk of collisions and causes more congestion.
options: Flash your hazard lights regularly
Tailgate the car in front to prevent others cutting in
Switch lanes frequently to find the fastest queue
Avoid changing lanes unnecessarily

bank.question: How will an empty roof rack affect your car's performance?
bank.explanation: A roof rack increases wind resistance, which makes the engine work harder and burns more fuel.
options: It makes the car more aerodynamic
It reduces the weight of the vehicle
It increases fuel consumption
It improves the car's acceleration

bank.question: You are following a vehicle on a wet, unlit night. What should you do?
bank.explanation: When following a vehicle on an unlit road, you must switch to dipped headlights to avoid dazzling the driver in front through their mirrors.
options: Keep your main beam on to see better
Switch to sidelights only
Flash your headlights periodically
Use dipped headlights

bank.question: You are following a cyclist and they start to move towards the centre of the road. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Cyclists may need to move to the middle of the road to turn right or to avoid hazards like potholes or car doors opening. Give them plenty of room.
options: Overtake them as quickly as possible
Sound your horn to tell them to move back to the left
Drive very closely behind them so they know you want to pass
Give them as much room as you would give a car

bank.question: Red reflective studs on a motorway are found between the acceleration lane and the main carriageway
bank.explanation: Red reflective studs are placed between the hard shoulder and the carriageway to help drivers identify the edge of the road in the dark.

bank.question: What does this sign tell you?
bank.explanation: An upright blue rectangle with a white arrow pointing up indicates a one-way street. Traffic is only permitted to travel in the direction of the arrow.
bank.imageAlt: A blue rectangular sign with a large white arrow pointing upwards
options: Straight ahead only at the next junction
The road ahead has a steep hill
One-way street ahead
Dual carriageway starts here

bank.question: When is it legal to park on the area marked by zigzag lines at a bus stop?
bank.explanation: Stopping at a bus stop can obstruct buses and put passengers at risk. You should never park or stop there unless signs permit it.
options: If you are just picking up a friend
If you stay with the vehicle
During the hours of darkness
Under no circumstances

bank.question: You are approaching a level crossing and the red lights start to flash. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Red flashing lights (sometimes called 'wig-wag' signals) at a level crossing mean you must stop and wait behind the stop line.
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop only if a train is clearly visible
Stop, then crawl forward to see if a train is coming
Stop before the stop line and wait

bank.question: What is meant by the term 'covering the brake'?
bank.explanation: Covering the brake means taking your foot off the accelerator and hovering it over the brake pedal to reduce your reaction time.
options: Braking hard to slow down quickly
Keeping your foot firmly on the accelerator
Taking your foot off the accelerator and hovering it over the brake
Applying the handbrake slightly while moving
