bank.question: When driving on a motorway at night, what colour are the reflective studs that mark the right-hand edge of the carriageway, next to the central reservation?
bank.explanation: Amber studs are consistently used to denote the boundary between the main carriageway and the central reservation on a motorway, guiding drivers on the far right.
options: Green
Red
White
Amber

bank.question: The main benefit of an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) is that it allows the driver to steer while braking heavily
bank.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent wheels from locking, allowing you to continue steering while braking hard in an emergency.

bank.question: How should you use this box junction?
bank.explanation: A yellow box marking at a junction is meant to keep the intersection clear. You should only enter it if your exit is clear, or if you are turning right and waiting for a gap.
bank.imageAlt: An intersection with yellow criss-cross lines painted on the tarmac
options: Always stop before entering the boxes
Do not enter unless your exit is clear
Only buses are allowed to stop in the box
Traffic from the right has priority over you

bank.question: Scanning the road ahead for potential hazards is an essential part of 'defensive driving'
bank.explanation: By looking ahead, you can anticipate hazards, react more smoothly, and avoid unnecessary braking or acceleration.

bank.question: You are parking your car facing downhill. How should you set your front wheels?
bank.explanation: When parking on a downhill slope, turning your wheels towards the kerb acts as a safety measure to prevent the car from rolling into traffic if the parking brake fails.
options: Turn them away from the kerb
Keep them perfectly straight
Turn them towards the kerb
Turn them to the right regardless of the kerb position

bank.question: Your tyre bursts while you are driving on the motorway. You stop on the hard shoulder. Where should you wait for help?
bank.explanation: If you have a puncture on the motorway, you should pull onto the hard shoulder, call for assistance, and wait behind the crash barrier for safety. Do not attempt to change the wheel yourself.
options: Change the wheel quickly on the hard shoulder
Try to reach the next service station
Wait in the car until help arrives
Wait behind the crash barrier until help arrives

bank.question: While driving at night on a well-lit built-up road, which headlights should you use?
bank.explanation: At night, you must use dipped headlights even on well-lit roads so that other road users can see you clearly. Keeping them dipped prevents dazzling others.
options: Full-beam headlights
Sidelights only
Dipped headlights
Fog lights

bank.question: When approaching a roundabout, to whom should you usually give way?
bank.explanation: When approaching a roundabout, you should give way to traffic coming from your right unless signs or markings indicate otherwise.
options: Traffic from the left
Traffic from the right
Emerging traffic from the opposite side
All traffic already on the roundabout, regardless of direction

bank.question: Why are there yellow zigzag lines on the road outside a school?
bank.explanation: Parking near a school entrance on yellow zigzag lines endangers children's lives by blocking visibility for both drivers and pedestrians.
options: To allow teachers easy access to the school
To keep the area clear so children can see and be seen safely
To provide a drop-off point for parents and children
To mark the area where the school bus stops

bank.question: What does ABS help you to do while braking hard?
bank.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent the wheels from locking, which allows the driver to maintain steering control during heavy braking.
options: Stop the vehicle in a much shorter distance
Allow the driver to steer while braking harshly
Prevent the vehicle from skidding on black ice
Apply the handbrake automatically in an emergency

bank.question: If you see a pedestrian with a dog wearing a yellow or burgundy coat, what does this indicate?
bank.explanation: If you see a pedestrian with a dog wearing a yellow or burgundy coat, they are likely to be deaf. A white cane with a red band indicates someone who is both deaf and blind.
options: Deaf
Blind
Physically disabled
Colour blind

bank.question: You are the first person to arrive at the scene of a crash. What is the first thing you should do?
bank.explanation: The first thing you should do when arriving at an incident scene is ensure your own safety and the safety of others by switching on your hazard lights.
options: Move the injured people away from their cars
Call your friends to tell them you will be late
Switch on your hazard warning lights
Try to move the damaged vehicles off the road

bank.question: When are you allowed to stop on the hard shoulder of a motorway?
bank.explanation: On a motorway, the hard shoulder is for emergencies and breakdowns only. You must not use it for rest or making phone calls.
options: Only in an emergency or breakdown
To answer a mobile phone call
If you feel tired and need to rest
To let faster traffic pass you

bank.question: Up to what height must a child use a suitable child restraint?
bank.explanation: The law requires all child passengers to use an appropriate child restraint unless they are over 135cm tall or 12 years old.
options: 125 cm
150 cm
135 cm
145 cm

bank.question: Which type of road user is most likely to be affected by side winds on an open stretch of road?
bank.explanation: In very windy weather, high-sided vehicles, cyclists, and motorcyclists are most at risk of being blown off course.
options: Tractor drivers
Large car drivers
Bus passengers
Motorcyclists and cyclists

bank.question: You are approaching a narrow bridge. What should you do?
bank.explanation: On narrow roads or bridges, you should always be prepared to give way to oncoming traffic to keep the flow of traffic moving and avoid a collision.
options: Sound your horn so people know you are coming
Speed up to reach the bridge first
Be prepared to give way to oncoming traffic
Switch on your hazard lights and stay in the middle of the road

bank.question: What does it mean if your vehicle's exhaust is puffing out blue smoke?
bank.explanation: Blue smoke is a sign that oil is being burned within the engine, which usually indicates worn engine components.
options: The air filter is blocked
The fuel is contaminated with water
The exhaust system has a hole
The engine is burning excess oil

bank.question: When are you allowed to use a handheld mobile phone while driving?
bank.explanation: Touching a mobile phone while driving - even if it is in your hand to look at a map - is illegal and highly distracting. Use a hands-free mount if necessary.
options: When you are stopped at a red traffic light
When you are in a slow-moving traffic queue
When you are pulled over on a hard shoulder to check a map
None of the above - you should never use a handheld phone while driving

bank.question: You are being followed closely by another vehicle. What should you do to reduce the risk of an accident?
bank.explanation: If someone is following you too closely (tailgating), increase your following distance from the vehicle in front so you can brake more gradually if needed.
options: Brake sharply to warn them to back off
Gradually increase your gap from the vehicle in front
Speed up to get away from them
Turn your hazard lights on to show your annoyance

bank.question: The safest way to negotiate a sharp bend is to brake firmly while you are turning the steering wheel
bank.explanation: Braking harder while cornering can cause the weight to shift and lead to a loss of grip or a skid; you should brake to the correct speed before entering the bend.

bank.question: How will a heavy load on your roof rack affect your car's performance?
bank.explanation: Heavy loads on a roof rack increase wind resistance and the vehicle's centre of gravity, significantly increasing fuel consumption.
options: It will improve the car's stability at high speeds
It will increase fuel consumption
It will make the car accelerate faster
It will reduce the pressure on the tyres

bank.question: In which of these places must you NOT park?
bank.explanation: Parking near the brow of a hill restricts the view for other drivers, making it dangerous to overtake or see oncoming traffic.
options: Where there is a dropped kerb
Near the brow of a hill
On a one-way street
In a marked parking bay

bank.question: Why should you be particularly careful of pedestrians when driving an electric vehicle?
bank.explanation: Electric vehicles are very quiet, making it difficult for pedestrians (especially those with visual impairments) to hear them approaching at low speeds.
options: They are very quiet when moving at low speeds
They have different coloured headlights
They are significantly wider than petrol cars
They always have the right of way

bank.question: How will your fuel consumption be affected when you are towing a trailer?
bank.explanation: Towing a trailer increases the load on the engine and creates more wind resistance, both of which lead to higher fuel consumption.
options: It reduces fuel consumption by smoothing airflow
It has no effect on fuel consumption if the trailer is empty
It will increase fuel consumption
It only increases fuel consumption on motorways

bank.question: While driving on a country road and see a sheep wandering on the highway, what should you do?
bank.explanation: If you see a sheep or horse on the road, stop and switch off your engine if necessary. Do not rev your engine or sound your horn as this could spook them.
options: Stop and switch off your engine if necessary
Sound your horn to clear the animal from the road
Rev your engine to encourage the animal to move
Slow down and flash your headlights repeatedly

bank.question: What does a green flashing beacon on a vehicle mean?
bank.explanation: Green flashes on a vehicle indicate that it is being driven by a doctor or medical professional attending an emergency.
options: A school bus picking up children
A slow-moving agricultural vehicle
A doctor on an emergency call
A gritter spreading salt on the road

bank.question: Where should you position your car when following a large vehicle?
bank.explanation: When following a large vehicle, stay well back so that the driver can see you in their mirrors and so you have a better view of the road ahead.
options: Close to the vehicle to stay in its slipstream
To the right-hand side of the lane to see past it
Close to the vehicle so the driver can see you better
Well back so that you can see the road ahead more clearly

bank.question: How should you drive when passing sheep or horses on a country road?
bank.explanation: When passing horses, drive slowly and give them plenty of room, as they are easily spooked by noise and proximity.
options: Sound your horn to alert the rider
Accelerate quickly to pass them as fast as possible
Drive slowly and leave plenty of room
Use your full beam headlights to see better around them

bank.question: What do long yellow lines painted across the road represent when approaching a hazard?
bank.explanation: Yellow lines across the road are typically found on the approach to roundabouts or dangerous junctions to encourage drivers to reduce their speed.
options: A change in the speed limit
The presence of a school crossing
A roundabout or dangerous junction ahead
A pedestrian zone entry site

bank.question: You may use your hazard warning lights to signal to other drivers that you are parked illegally
bank.explanation: Hazard lights should only be used while driving to warn following traffic of a hazard or obstruction ahead on a motorway or unrestricted dual carriageway.

bank.question: On a motorway, what do white reflective studs signify?
bank.explanation: White studs are used to mark the lanes or the middle of the road on motorways and dual carriageways.
options: The left-hand edge of the road
The lane markings between lanes
The right-hand edge of the road (next to the central reservation)
The entrance or exit to slip roads

bank.question: When should you use a handheld mobile phone while driving?
bank.explanation: Touching a mobile phone, even if it is for navigation, is illegal while driving. Always set your route before you start your journey.
options: When the road is clear and straight
When you are stopped at red traffic lights
When you are driving at less than 30 mph
Never while you are driving

bank.question: How far back from a junction should you avoid parking?
bank.explanation: Parking within 10 metres of a junction reduces visibility for other drivers and makes it harder for large vehicles to turn.
options: 10 metres (32 feet)
2 metres (7 feet)
20 metres (66 feet)
5 metres (16 feet)

bank.question: What hazard does this warning sign show?
bank.explanation: This warning sign means there is an opening or swing bridge ahead. Slow down and be prepared to stop if the bridge is opening, closing, or controlled by traffic signals.
bank.imageAlt: Triangular warning sign for an opening or swing bridge ahead
options: Roadside ford
Approaching tower bridge
Opening or swing bridge
Electric fence

bank.question: When using a jack to change a wheel, you should apply the parking brake and put the car in gear before lifting the vehicle
bank.explanation: Before using a jack, apply the parking brake and put the car in gear or in Park. This helps prevent the vehicle from moving while it is being raised.

bank.question: What does it mean if an area of the road is marked with white diagonal stripes and bounded by a solid white line?
bank.explanation: Hatching with a solid boundary line means you must not enter the area except in an emergency. If the boundary is broken, you should not enter unless it is necessary and safe.
options: You can use it to overtake slow-moving lorries
You must use it when turning right at a junction
You can park there if there are no yellow lines
You must not enter the area except in an emergency

bank.question: If your car breaks down on a motorway, what is the safest way to call for help?
bank.explanation: In any emergency or breakdown on a motorway, you should use the emergency telephone to call for help, as it connects directly to the authorities and identifies your location.
options: Your mobile phone to call a friend
A passing motorist for a lift
The emergency roadside telephone to contact Highways England or the police
A flare to signal for help

bank.question: What does this sign indicate?
bank.explanation: Clearways are stretches of road where stopping is prohibited at all times to keep traffic moving freely.
bank.imageAlt: A blue circular sign with a red cross and a red border
options: No stopping (Clearway)
No waiting
No entry for motor vehicles
National speed limit applies

bank.question: What is a 'High-Occupancy Vehicle lane' (HOV lane)?
bank.explanation: High-occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes are designed to encourage car-sharing. They can only be used by vehicles carrying at least the number of people shown on the sign.
options: Only for HGVs and heavy machinery
Only for emergency vehicles and buses
Reserved for vehicles with no passengers (driver only)
Reserved for vehicles with the minimum number of people shown on the sign

bank.question: When driving down a steep, narrow urban street with vehicles parked on either side, what is the most effective way to control your speed and prevent your brakes from overheating?
bank.explanation: Selecting a low gear uses the engine to help slow the vehicle, known as engine braking. This reduces the need to use the footbrake, preventing it from overheating and becoming less effective (brake fade).
options: Coast by putting the clutch down and only using the footbrake.
Gently apply the handbrake to maintain a steady, slow speed.
Keep the car in a high gear to ensure the engine runs quietly.
Select a low gear and use the footbrake carefully when needed.

bank.question: When may you stop in an emergency refuge area on a motorway?
bank.explanation: Stopping at an emergency refuge area is only permitted in an actual emergency or if your vehicle breaks down. Drivers should never use it for rest.
options: To check a map or use a phone
If your vehicle breaks down
To take a rest break if you feel tired
To pick up a hitchhiker

bank.question: You have just driven through a deep puddle. What is the best way to dry your brakes?
bank.explanation: To dry out wet brakes after driving through a deep puddle, you should drive slowly and apply light pressure to the brake pedal.
options: Drive at high speed to blow the water off
Apply light pressure to the brakes while driving slowly
Stop the car and wait 15 minutes for them to dry naturally
Pump the accelerator pedal repeatedly

bank.question: To drive helpfully and safely, where should you mainly be looking?
bank.explanation: The 'long-range' view is the most important for anticipating hazards and planning your driving path effectively.
options: The vehicle's instrument panel
The area immediately in front of your bonnet
The road far ahead to anticipate hazards
The interior and exterior mirrors only

bank.question: How can you avoid wheel spin when driving on an icy road?
bank.explanation: When moving off on a snowy or icy road, using a higher gear (such as second) helps to reduce wheel spin by applying less torque to the wheels.
options: Use the highest gear possible and high engine revs
Use a higher gear than normal with low engine revs
Use the lowest gear possible with high engine revs
Keep the handbrake partially on to create friction

bank.question: What happens to stopping distances in wet weather?
bank.explanation: Stopping distances are roughly double in wet weather because there is less grip between the tyres and the road surface.
options: They stay exactly the same
They are four times longer than on a dry road
They are at least double the distance on a dry road
They are slightly shorter if you have winter tyres

bank.question: It is legal to enter a yellow box junction to turn right if your exit is clear but you are blocked by oncoming traffic
bank.explanation: At a box junction, you may enter the box and wait if you want to turn right and are only prevented from doing so by oncoming traffic or other vehicles waiting to turn right.

bank.question: You are behind a large vehicle approaching a left-hand turn. Why might the driver move out to the right side of the road?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles need more room to turn. They may swing out to the right before turning left to ensure the rear wheels don't hit the kerb.
options: The driver has changed their mind
The vehicle needs more room to turn
The driver is waiting for a pedestrian to cross
The vehicle is about to turn right

bank.question: On a motorway, amber reflective studs are used to mark the boundary between the left-hand lane and the hard shoulder
bank.explanation: Amber reflective studs are used to mark the edge of the carriageway next to the central reservation, not the hard shoulder.

bank.question: Who has priority at an unmarked crossroads?
bank.explanation: The priority at an unmarked crossroads is for nobody; you must proceed with extreme caution and look out for others.
options: The vehicle on the wider road
No one has priority; you must be careful and prepared to stop
Traffic travelling straight ahead only
The vehicle moving at the fastest speed

bank.question: How will a heavy load carry on a roof rack affect your car's handling?
bank.explanation: Heavy loads can affect the vehicle's stability and increase fuel consumption. They also increase the distance needed to stop.
options: It will increase the stopping distance
It will improve the road grip on bends
It will decrease the fuel consumption
It will shorten the braking distance

bank.question: On a road marked as a 'Clearway', what are the stopping restrictions?
bank.explanation: Stopping on a clearway is prohibited to ensure the free flow of traffic. You must not stop at any time, even briefly to pick up passengers.
options: You can stop for a maximum of 2 minutes
You can stop to pick up or drop off passengers
You must not stop at any time
You can stop if there are no other cars around

bank.question: When driving on a narrow road with cars parked on the left, what should you do if a car is approaching from the opposite direction?
bank.explanation: Even if your side of the road is clear, you should slow down and be prepared to stop if traffic from the other side is narrowed by parked cars.
options: Speed up to get through the gap quickly
Slow down and be prepared to give way
Flash your lights to claim your right of way
Drive onto the pavement to create more space

bank.question: If you have been driving through deep snow or slush, what is the best way to clear ice from your brakes?
bank.explanation: In very cold weather, moisture can freeze on the brake pads or shoes. Lightly using the brakes while driving slowly can help dry and warm them.
options: Drive as fast as possible to create heat
Use the handbrake frequently while moving
Apply the brakes lightly while driving slowly
Wait for the engine to reach its full temperature

bank.question: How often should you check your tyre pressures?
bank.explanation: To prevent a puncture or blowout, you should check your tyre pressures at least once a week when the tyres are cold for an accurate reading.
options: At least once a week when the tyres are cold
Every time you stop for fuel while the tyres are hot
Once every six months during a service
Only when the steering starts to vibrate

bank.question: Which lane should you normally use when driving on a three-lane motorway?
bank.explanation: On a motorway, you should normally use the left-hand lane unless you are overtaking slower-moving vehicles.
options: The right-hand lane
The middle lane
Any lane that is free
The left-hand lane

bank.question: You only need to inform the police, not the DVLA, if your eyesight deteriorates to below the legal driving standard
bank.explanation: You must notify the DVLA if you develop a condition that affects your eyesight, or if your eyesight deteriorates to a level where it does not meet the legal standard.

bank.question: Which lights should you use when driving on a well-lit motorway at night?
bank.explanation: At night, use dipped headlights when following other vehicles or meeting oncoming traffic to avoid dazzling other drivers.
options: Side lights only
Dipped headlights
Full beam headlights
Fog lights

bank.question: You are towing a small trailer on a dual carriageway. It begins to swerve or 'snake'. What should you do?
bank.explanation: If a trailer starts to swerve (snake), you should ease off the accelerator slowly to allow the vehicle to regain stability.
options: Ease off the accelerator and reduce speed gradually
Brake hard and steer in the opposite direction
Accelerate quickly to pull the trailer straight
Shift into neutral and coast to a stop

bank.question: On a standard road, what does it mean when the white lines in the centre of the road become longer and the gaps between them become shorter?
bank.explanation: White lines with long gaps and short markings are standard lane markings. When the gaps become shorter and the white lines become longer, it indicates a hazard is ahead.
options: A bus lane starts ahead
The road is about to become a dual carriageway
A hazard is ahead
Overtaking is permitted for the next mile

bank.question: You are approaching a narrow bridge where there are no signs. What should you do if there is a car coming towards you?
bank.explanation: You should give way to oncoming traffic when you see the sign indicating that traffic from the opposite direction has priority.
options: Flash your lights to show you are coming through
Speed up to get through the narrow section first
Give way to oncoming traffic
Drive onto the pavement to make room

bank.question: Carrying a heavy load in your vehicle can significantly increase your overall braking distance
bank.explanation: Heavy loads can increase the distance it takes to stop and affect the way the vehicle handles when cornering.

bank.question: How should you drive when going down a long, steep hill?
bank.explanation: Always use a low gear when descending a steep hill. The engine will help control your speed, preventing the brakes from overheating and fading.
options: High gear and light braking
Lower gear and use the engine to help control speed
Stay in neutral to save fuel
Keep the clutch depressed throughout the descent

bank.question: An MOT certificate for a car is valid for two years from the date of issue
bank.explanation: A car's MOT certificate is valid for 12 months (one year) from the date of the test.

bank.question: At traffic lights, what does it mean if a green filter arrow shows at the same time as a red light?
bank.explanation: A green filter arrow at a traffic light means you may proceed in the direction of the arrow, even if the main green light is not lit.
options: Wait for the main green light to show
Proceed in the direction of the arrow
Stop and wait for the light to turn amber
Only turn if there is no other traffic in any direction

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: When you see this sign, you must give way to oncoming traffic that is already in the narrowed section of the road.
bank.imageAlt: A circular sign with a red border. Inside, there is a large red arrow pointing up and a smaller black arrow pointing down
options: You have priority over oncoming vehicles
No motor vehicles allowed
Give way to oncoming traffic
Only buses and cycles may pass

bank.question: What must you do if you are involved in a collision that causes damage to another vehicle?
bank.explanation: If you are involved in a collision that causes damage, you must stop at the scene and exchange details with anyone else involved.
options: Stop and give your name and address to anyone involved
Drive to the nearest police station within 24 hours
Only stop if someone appears to be injured
Call your insurance company before exiting the car

bank.question: What does a circular road sign with a blue background usually mean?
bank.explanation: Blue circles with a white border generally give instructions or indicate a mandatory requirement, such as 'turn left'.
options: Warning of a hazard ahead
Information about a local destination
A prohibition, such as 'no entry'
Giving an instruction or mandatory direction

bank.question: What does the safety system 'ESC' stand for?
bank.explanation: Electronic Stability Control (ESC) helps prevent skids by detecting when a driver is losing control and applying brakes to individual wheels.
options: Engine Speed Control
Emergency Stopping Calibration
Electric Steering Check
Electronic Stability Control

bank.question: What is a common cause of 'brake fade'?
bank.explanation: Brake fade occurs when the brakes become too hot, often caused by heavy use on long downhill stretches, reducing their effectiveness.
options: The brake fluid level is too high
The tyres are worn beyond the legal limit
The brakes have overheated
The road surface is uneven

bank.question: What information must you give if you are involved in a collision that causes damage to another vehicle?
bank.explanation: If you have a collision, you must provide your name, address, and vehicle registration to anyone having reasonable grounds for requiring them.
options: Your driving licence number and MOT certificate
Your name, address, and vehicle registration number
Your insurance policy number and telephone number
Your date of birth and National Insurance number

bank.question: In which of these situations are you allowed to stop on a clearway?
bank.explanation: You must never stop or park on a clearway during its hours of operation, even to set down or pick up passengers, as it is designed to keep traffic flowing.
options: Pick up a passenger who is waiting
Check a map if you are lost
Answer a call on your mobile phone
Break down or have an emergency stop

bank.question: A car following you with a flashing blue light may be a doctor on an emergency call
bank.explanation: Blue flashing lights on a vehicle that isn't a standard 'emergency service' vehicle (like a car) typically indicate a doctor answering an emergency call.

bank.question: While driving in heavy rain during the day, what should you do to stay safe?
bank.explanation: Dipped headlights should be used in poor daytime visibility, such as heavy rain or fog, to help other road users see you.
options: Use dipped headlights
Use sidelights only
Use rear fog lights only
Use hazard warning lights

bank.question: You see a large vehicle ahead signalling left but moving to the right. Why might this be?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles often need extra room to negotiate tight turns. If they are turning left, they may need to swing out to the right first.
options: The driver has changed their mind and is turning right
The driver is about to stop and park on the right
The driver is flashing you to overtake on the left
The vehicle may need to swing out to the right to complete the turn

bank.question: How long is a SORN (Statutory Off Road Notification) valid for?
bank.explanation: The SORN (Statutory Off Road Notification) is valid until the vehicle is taxed, sold, or scrapped. It no longer needs annual renewal.
options: Until the vehicle is taxed, sold, or scrapped
For exactly 12 months only
Until the vehicle passes its next MOT
For the duration of your insurance policy

bank.question: A steady red light and a steady amber light showing together at a traffic signal mean you must wait and not pass the line
bank.explanation: When an amber light follows red, it means you should prepare to go but do not move until the light turns green.

bank.question: How can using a hands-free mobile phone affect your driving?
bank.explanation: Using your mobile phone, even with a hands-free kit, can significantly distract you from the road and slow your reaction times.
options: It will improve your concentration
It will distract your attention from the road
It is safe as long as you drive slowly
It will help you stay awake on long journeys

bank.question: What does 'covering the brake' mean?
bank.explanation: The 'Cover the Brake' technique involves hovering your foot over the brake pedal without pressing it, which can save vital milliseconds in an emergency.
options: Covering the brake pedal with your foot to reduce reaction time
Applying the handbrake while the vehicle is still moving
Hard braking just before a corner
Pumping the brake pedal to clear water from the discs

bank.question: What does it mean if a bus lane sign shows no times of operation?
bank.explanation: A bus lane sign with no times indicated means that the bus lane is in operation 24 hours a day, and you may not drive in it.
options: It is only in use during rush hour
It is in operation 24 hours a day
It is for use by any vehicle with more than one occupant
It is currently closed for roadworks

bank.question: You want to turn your vehicle around. Which of these movements is prohibited?
bank.explanation: You should never reverse from a side road into a main road; it is dangerous for both you and other road users. Always reverse from the main road into a minor road.
options: Reverse from a side road into a main road
Reverse from a main road into a side road bypass
Drive into a side road and turn around using a driveway
Drive around the block using three left turns

bank.question: Which type of vehicle uses a flashing green beacon?
bank.explanation: A flashing green light on a vehicle indicates that a doctor or medical professional is responding to an emergency call. Give way if it is safe to do so.
options: A breakdown recovery truck
A wide load escort vehicle
A doctor responding to an emergency
A coastguard vehicle

bank.question: When should you check your mirrors?
bank.explanation: You should check your mirrors before every manoeuvre, including changing speed, to see how your actions will affect traffic behind.
options: Just before you start to brake hard
Before any change in speed or direction
Only when you intend to pull over to the left
When you are about to accelerate into a higher gear

bank.question: When should you use your rear fog lights?
bank.explanation: Fog lights should only be used when visibility is seriously reduced (less than 100 metres) as they can dazzle other drivers.
options: When visibility is reduced to less than 100 metres
Whenever it is raining heavily at night
When you are driving on a narrow country lane
If you are being followed too closely by another car

bank.question: You are approaching a level crossing that has no gates or barriers. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Level crossings with no gates or barriers are extremely dangerous; you must always be prepared to stop if the lights flash.
options: Always be prepared to stop if the lights flash
Speed up to cross the tracks as quickly as possible
Stop only if you can see a train approaching
Treat it like a normal road junction and proceed slowly

bank.question: When should you avoid braking while driving around a bend?
bank.explanation: Braking when your vehicle is on a bend makes it less stable. It is safer to brake to the correct speed before you enter the turn.
options: In the middle of the bend to stay safe
Before you enter the bend
Just as you are exiting the bend
Only if you feel the car sliding

bank.question: What is a primary benefit of having tyres with deep tread?
bank.explanation: Deep tread is essential for tyres to disperse water on wet roads, reducing the risk of aquaplaning.
options: Fuel economy will be greatly improved
The risk of aquaplaning will be reduced
The vehicle's top speed will increase
The steering will feel much lighter

bank.question: What does this blue mandatory sign mean?
bank.explanation: This blue mandatory sign means you must keep left of the sign or obstruction. Do not pass to the right of it unless directed by a police officer or traffic management.
bank.imageAlt: Blue circular Keep Left sign with a white arrow pointing down-left
options: Turn left ahead only
No entry to the left
Keep right at all times
Keep left

bank.question: Using a lower gear when driving down a steep, slippery hill will?
bank.explanation: Braking on a slippery road can lead to skidding. Engine braking (shifting to a lower gear) uses the engine's compression to slow the car down more safely.
options: Help you stay in control of the vehicle
Increase the speed of your car downhill
Prevent the engine from overheating
Make the steering feel lighter and easier

bank.question: How might carrying a heavy load affect your vehicle's lights?
bank.explanation: A heavy load will increase the weight at the rear, causing the front of the car to rise and your headlights to aim higher, potentially dazzling others.
options: The vehicle will accelerate much faster
The steering will feel much heavier
The gear changes will become shorter
The headlights may aim too high and dazzle others

bank.question: You may pass a vehicle on the left if you are in a queue of traffic that is moving faster than the queue to your right
bank.explanation: Overtaking on the left (undertaking) is generally not allowed, but it is acceptable in slow-moving queues of traffic where your lane is moving faster than the lane to your right.

bank.question: Who must you notify if your health changes in a way that affects your driving?
bank.explanation: You must inform the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) if your eyesight deteriorates or if you develop a reportable medical condition.
options: Your local GP surgery
The police station nearest your home
The DVLA (Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency)
Your insurance company only

bank.question: You have just driven through deep water. What is the first thing you should do when clear of the water?
bank.explanation: Touching the brake pedal lightly (feathering) will generate heat through friction, which helps dry out the brake pads and discs.
options: Switch on your hazard lights
Accelerate quickly to spin the water off
Pump the clutch pedal repeatedly
Go slowly and brake lightly to dry them out

bank.question: You see a sign at a level crossing with three red diagonal lines on a white background. What does this mean?
bank.explanation: Countdown markers at level crossings use red diagonal bars on a white background. Three bars mean the crossing is about 300 yards away; each bar represents roughly 100 yards.
options: You are 300 yards from the level crossing
There are three railway tracks to cross
The train will arrive in three minutes
Only three vehicles are allowed to cross at once

bank.question: You see a pedestrian carrying a white stick with a red band. What does this mean?
bank.explanation: If you see a pedestrian with a white stick that has a red band, it means they are both deaf and blind. Give them plenty of room.
options: The pedestrian is blind only
The pedestrian is deaf and blind
The pedestrian is physically disabled
The pedestrian is deaf only

bank.question: When should you use the horn of your vehicle?
bank.explanation: You should use your horn only to warn other road users of your presence and potential danger. Never use it to show annoyance.
options: To greet friends in other cars
To signal your annoyance at another driver's mistake
To let a driver know you are giving way to them
To warn other road users of your presence and potential danger

bank.question: You are following a long lorry approaching a left-hand turn. Why should you stay well back?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles like lorries need more room to turn and may swing out to the right before turning left into a narrow side road.
options: The vehicle may swing out to the right before turning
The vehicle will speed up to clear the junction quickly
The driver will always stop before making the turn
The indicators will flash much faster than usual

bank.question: Which part of the road is most likely to freeze first in cold weather?
bank.explanation: When temperatures drop, bridges and overpasses freeze first because they are exposed to air on both top and bottom.
options: Bridges and overpasses
Roads in busy town centres
Roads that have been gritted recently
Stretch of road near a motorway junction

bank.question: On some bridges, the maximum height shown on the sign may only apply to the highest part of the arch
bank.explanation: At some arched bridges, the signed height may apply only to the highest part of the arch. Tall vehicles should keep to the marked route and obey any lane-specific height signs.

bank.question: When should you check the tyre pressures of your vehicle?
bank.explanation: You should check your tyre pressures when they are cold, as heat generated from driving can increase the pressure and give an inaccurate reading.
options: After a long motorway journey
When the tyres are cold
After the car has been parked in the sun
Immediately after a high-speed drive

bank.question: When must you notify the DVLA that you have a Statutory Off-Road Notification (SORN)?
bank.explanation: A SORN must be made if a vehicle is not being used on public roads and is not taxed or insured.
options: The vehicle is being kept in a garage and is taxed
The vehicle is parked on a public highway
The vehicle is used only for short trips
The vehicle is not being used on the road and is not taxed

bank.question: Why should you be particularly cautious when driving near trams?
bank.explanation: Tram drivers cannot steer to avoid you, so they are given priority at many junctions. Always look out for tram-specific signals.
options: They cannot steer to avoid obstructions
They always have a higher speed limit than cars
They have the right of way by law at all times
They are much heavier and take longer to stop

bank.question: What does this sign warn you about?
bank.explanation: When you see a 'slippery road' sign, you should reduce your speed and avoid sudden braking or steering to prevent a skid.
bank.imageAlt: A triangular warning sign with a car skidding symbol
options: No motor vehicles allowed due to ice
A steep hill downwards ahead
A car testing area only
The road surface ahead may be slippery

bank.question: When driving in a tunnel and your vehicle breaks down, what is the first thing you should do?
bank.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down in a tunnel, switch on your hazard lights and then call for help from an emergency telephone point.
options: Walk out of the tunnel to find a signal for your mobile phone
Switch on your hazard lights and use an emergency telephone
Stay in the car and wait for a patrol vehicle to find you
Attempt to fix the fault yourself immediately

bank.question: How can you tell if your car is aquaplaning?
bank.explanation: Heavy rain can lead to aquaplaning, where your tyres lose contact with the road and slide on a thin film of water. If this happens, ease off the accelerator to slow down.
options: The steering will feel light
The steering will feel very heavy
The engine will suddenly cut out
The brakes will lock automatically

bank.question: In which situation should you give extra room to the vehicle in front?
bank.explanation: In high winds, large vehicles and motorcyclists are particularly vulnerable to being blown off course. Give them extra room.
options: When it is raining heavily
When you are driving at night
When you are following a cyclist on a calm day
When you are overtaking a high-sided vehicle on a windy day

bank.question: What part of your car can cause a blind spot and hide a motorcyclist at a junction?
bank.explanation: The 'Sizzly' technique or moving from side to side can help you see around the 'A' pillars of the car (the frames around the windscreen) which can block your view of pedestrians or cyclists.
options: Framing of the windscreen (windscreen pillars)
The interior rear-view mirror
The passenger in the front seat
The bonnet of your car

bank.question: You should use your rear fog lights whenever it is raining to make your car more visible
bank.explanation: Fog lights should only be used when visibility is seriously reduced (generally less than 100 metres) as they can dazzle other road users.

bank.question: What does a single solid white line along the side of the road mean?
bank.explanation: On national speed limit roads, a single solid white line along the side signifies the edge of the carriageway. It helps drivers identify the road limit in poor visibility.
options: The start of a cycle lane
A hazard warning for a junction ahead
Clearance for parking is allowed here
The edge of the carriageway

bank.question: How can a heavy cold or flu affect your driving?
bank.explanation: When you are cold or have a fever, your concentration levels drop and your reaction times increase, making driving more dangerous.
options: It will help you stay awake and alert
It will make you drive more slowly and safely
It can slow down your reactions and reduce concentration
It won't affect your driving as long as you take medicine

bank.question: When is the safest time to brake when you are approaching a sharp bend?
bank.explanation: Braking while cornering can cause the car to lose stability or skid. It is safer to slow down to the correct speed before you reach the bend.
options: Halfway through the bend
Just as you enter the bend
Before you reach the bend
When you are exiting the bend

bank.question: What is a particular risk to be aware of when driving an electric vehicle in a busy town?
bank.explanation: Electric vehicles are virtually silent at low speeds, making them harder for pedestrians and cyclists to hear.
options: They are much quieter than petrol or diesel cars
They have a much longer braking distance
They always have the right of way at junctions
They are not allowed to use cycle lanes

bank.question: Who has priority at a crossroads where there are no signs or road markings?
bank.explanation: At a crossroads with no signs or markings, no one has priority. You must slow down and look both ways before proceeding.
options: Vehicles on the wider road
No one has priority
Vehicles coming from the right
Vehicles coming from the left

bank.question: If you stop at a pedestrian crossing, it is a safe practice to wave pedestrians across to show them it is clear
bank.explanation: You should never wave pedestrians across the road; there may be another vehicle coming that you haven't seen, or they may be encouraged into danger.

bank.question: It is acceptable to use your horn to signal your frustration if another driver pulls out in front of you
bank.explanation: You should use your horn only to warn other road users of your presence or a potential danger, not to show annoyance or 'greet' others.

bank.question: You are approaching a hump bridge. What should you do?
bank.explanation: When approaching a hump bridge, you should slow down and stay cautious as they are often narrow and have very limited visibility.
options: Slow down and be prepared to stop
Speed up to get over it quickly
Stay in the middle of the road to see better
Keep your speed constant and sound your horn

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: A red circle with a car and a motorcycle means no motor vehicles are allowed. Pedestrians and cyclists may still use the route.
bank.imageAlt: A circular road sign with a red border containing a silhouette of a car and a motorcycle
options: No cars allowed
No motorcycles allowed
No motor vehicles allowed
Parking for motor vehicles only

bank.question: Which part of the car is designed to absorb the impact during a collision?
bank.explanation: Modern vehicles have a 'crumple zone' at the front and rear designed to absorb the energy of an impact, protecting the occupants.
options: The engine compartment
The crumple zone
The fuel tank housing
The alloy wheels

bank.question: What is meant by the term 'blind spot'?
bank.explanation: The 'blind spot' is an area around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors. You must check this by looking over your shoulder before moving off or changing lanes.
options: An area not visible in your mirrors
An area of the road covered by your headlights
The area directly in front of your bumper
The area covered by your rearview mirror only

bank.question: What do circular road signs with a red border generally represent?
bank.explanation: Circular signs with red borders give orders; they generally tell you things you must not do.
options: Give information about facilities ahead
Give orders that you must obey
Warn you of hazards ahead
Give directions to local destinations

bank.question: Which vehicles are occasionally exempt from a 'No Entry' sign if indicated by a sub-plate?
bank.explanation: Underneath a 'No Entry' sign, a plate may state 'Except cycles' or 'Except buses', allowing those specific vehicles to enter.
options: Taxis
Emergency vehicles
Motorcycles under 125cc
Buses or cycles if a plate indicates so

bank.question: In icy conditions, how much can your braking distance increase by?
bank.explanation: Braking distances are roughly ten times longer on icy or snowy roads compared to dry ones.
options: Ten times the normal distance
Twice the normal distance
Five times the normal distance
The same as the normal distance

bank.question: You want to turn right from a main road into a side road. There are pedestrians crossing the side road. What should you do?
bank.explanation: When turning from a main road into a side road, you should check your mirrors, signal, and slow down. Pedestrians already crossing the mouth of the side road have priority.
options: Wave them across the road quickly
Sound your horn to warn them you are turning in
Speed up to get into the side road before they cross
Wait and give way to them

bank.question: Why are some roads marked as 'Red Routes'?
bank.explanation: Red routes are marked with red lines to discourage stopping, keeping traffic flowing on busy urban roads.
options: To provide extra parking for residents
To allow lorries to load and unload anytime
To help the flow of traffic by restricting stopping
To mark out areas where cycle lanes begin

bank.question: What's the primary purpose of your vehicle's horn?
bank.explanation: Horns should primarily be used to warn other road users of your presence. They should not be used between 11:30 pm and 7:00 am in built-up areas.
options: To greet other drivers you know
To show your annoyance at a driver's mistake
To warn others of your presence
To signal your right of way at a junction

bank.question: Why should you avoid heavy braking while you are cornering?
bank.explanation: Braking and steering simultaneously when your car doesn't have ABS can cause the wheels to lock, leading to a loss of control. Strong braking should be done in a straight line before the turn.
options: It can cause your wheels to lock and the car to skid
It will cause the engine to stall unexpectedly
It significantly reduces the wear on your tyres
It helps the car grip the road better in the rain

bank.question: How can you help prevent your brakes from overheating when driving down a long, steep hill?
bank.explanation: Excessive heat from constant braking can cause 'brake fade,' making them less effective. Using a lower gear (engine braking) helps prevent this.
options: By using a lower gear to assist with braking
By pumping the footbrake repeatedly
By shifting into neutral to let the brakes cool down
By zigzagging within your lane to increase air flow

bank.question: What is 'brake fade' usually caused by?
bank.explanation: Brake fade occurs when brakes overheat, often during long descents. Using a lower gear provides engine braking to help prevent this.
options: Your brakes are cold and need to warm up
Your brakes have overheated
The brake fluid level is too high
The brake pads are brand new

bank.question: What is a common cause of collisions on motorways?
bank.explanation: Following too closely (tailgating) is the primary cause of many collisions, especially on high-speed roads where stopping distances are greater.
options: Driving too slowly
Using the mirrors too often
Following other vehicles too closely
Staying in the left-hand lane

bank.question: How should you treat a casualty who has a nosebleed?
bank.explanation: Tipping the head back can block the airway. Instead, you should lean the casualty forward and pinch the soft part of the nose.
options: Tip their head back as far as possible
Tell them to blow their nose hard
Apply a hot compress to the nose
Pinch the soft part of the nose and lean forward

bank.question: On a smart motorway, what does it mean when a mandatory speed limit is displayed above the hard shoulder?
bank.explanation: On some smart motorways, the hard shoulder can be opened as a running lane. You may use it only when a mandatory speed limit is displayed above the hard shoulder. If a red X is shown, or no signal is displayed above it, do not use it except in an emergency.
options: The hard shoulder is for emergency use only
You must pull over immediately
The hard shoulder can be used as a running lane
The motorway is closed ahead

bank.question: You see an elderly person crossing the road ahead. They are walking slowly. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Wait for the pedestrian to cross the road completely. Do not wave them across or rev your engine, as this may intimidate them.
options: Wave them across the road to show it is safe
Rev your engine to let them know you are waiting
Wait patiently and allow them to finish crossing
Edge forward slowly to encourage them to walk faster

bank.question: What does a steady amber light mean at a traffic signal?
bank.explanation: An amber light on its own means 'Stop' at the stop line unless you have already crossed it or are so close that stopping would cause an accident.
options: Go if the way is clear
Speed up to beat the red light
Stop at the stop line unless it is unsafe to do so
Wait for the green light to appear before proceeding

bank.question: How is the glass in a modern car windscreen designed to break?
bank.explanation: Toughened glass or safety glass in a windscreen is designed to break into small, rounded pieces rather than sharp shards to prevent serious injury during an accident.
options: It shatters into small, rounded pieces
It does not break at all
It breaks into long, sharp shards
It turns into a fine powder

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: This sign indicates a mandatory speed limit. You must not exceed 40 mph in this area.
bank.imageAlt: Circular 40 mph maximum speed limit sign
options: Recommended speed of 40 mph
Minimum speed of 40 mph
End of 40 mph zone
Maximum speed limit of 40 mph

bank.question: If you are driving uphill and there are parked cars on your side of the road, what should you do if there is oncoming traffic?
bank.explanation: Waiting at the end of the road allows the vehicles coming down the hill to pass, as they have a more difficult time stopping and starting.
options: Flash your lights to tell them to stop
Wait and give way to the vehicles coming downhill
Speed up to get through the gap first
Drive onto the pavement to make room

bank.question: When is the safest time to programme a destination into your satellite navigation system?
bank.explanation: A touch-screen navigation system can be a major distraction. It is best to input your destination before you start your journey.
options: While driving at high speeds
When you are stationary at traffic lights
Before you start your journey
While driving on a straight road

bank.question: What does a solid white line at the edge of the road mean?
bank.explanation: Solid white lines on the road are usually used to separate traffic or mark the edge of the road; a solid white line at the edge specifically indicates the road's boundary.
options: The edge of the carriageway
A hazard warning ahead
The approach to a roundabout
A no-parking zone

bank.question: How can you help prevent 'tailgating' (driving too close to the vehicle in front)?
bank.explanation: Keeping a safe gap between you and the vehicle in front is the best way to avoid a collision if they stop suddenly.
options: Stay very close to discourage them from braking
Flash your headlights to warn them you are there
Drive at a higher speed so you can pass them quickly
Keep a safe following distance from the vehicle in front

bank.question: When approaching a stationary hybrid vehicle, you should be aware that it may move off silently using electric power
bank.explanation: In some hybrid or electric vehicles, the engine may restart silently and the vehicle can move off without warning.

bank.question: What does a triangular road sign with a red border generally represent?
bank.explanation: A triangular road sign with a red border is a warning sign, alerting you to potential hazards ahead.
options: A speed limit or prohibition
A direction to a primary route
Information about parking facilities
A warning of a hazard ahead

bank.question: If you develop a medical condition that affects your driving, you only need to tell the DVLA if you intend to drive in the next 30 days
bank.explanation: You must notify the DVLA of any health condition that may affect your ability to drive safely, even if you do not plan to drive immediately.

bank.question: You are at a box junction. When may you enter it?
bank.explanation: The box junction is designed to keep the intersection clear; you must not enter unless your exit road is clear.
options: Wait behind the line until the lights change to amber
Continue through as long as you can see the lights are green
Wait until your exit road is clear before entering
Stop in the middle of the box to wait for a gap in traffic

bank.question: Diamond-shaped traffic signs are used to give instructions to lorry drivers regarding weight limits
bank.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs provide instructions specifically for tram drivers, though other road users should be aware of them.

bank.question: When driving at night on a well-lit road in a built-up area, which lights should you normally use?
bank.explanation: In well-lit built-up areas, dipped headlights ensure you are seen by other road users without dazzling them. Fog lights should only be used in seriously reduced visibility.
options: Full-beam headlights
Dipped headlights
Side lights only
Rear fog lights

bank.question: You are allowed to park your car on the pavement at any time as long as you leave enough room for a wheelchair to pass
bank.explanation: In some areas, such as London, parking on the pavement is strictly prohibited unless signs say otherwise. Generally, it should be avoided as it obstructs pedestrians.

bank.question: In which direction should you park your car at night on a two-way road?
bank.explanation: When vehicles are parked on the road at night, they must face in the direction of the traffic flow so that their rear reflectors can be seen by approaching drivers.
options: Facing the same direction as the traffic flow
Facing against the direction of the traffic flow
With the front wheels turned towards the kerb
In any direction as long as side lights are on

bank.question: When may you use the hard shoulder of a motorway?
bank.explanation: The hard shoulder must be kept clear for emergencies and breakdowns. You should never use it for resting or map reading.
options: To take a rest if you feel tired
In an emergency or breakdown
To pick up a hitchhiker
To check a map or use a smartphone

bank.question: Why should you use dipped headlights when following another vehicle at night?
bank.explanation: Dipping your lights when following or meeting other vehicles prevents you from dazzling the other drivers.
options: To save battery power
To avoid dazzling other road users
To see the road more clearly
To signal that you are following them

bank.question: What colour are the reflective studs between the hard shoulder and the left-hand lane of a motorway?
bank.explanation: On motorways, reflective studs between the hard shoulder and the carriageway are red. They help drivers see the edge of the road in the dark or in poor visibility.
options: Red
White
Amber
Green

bank.question: You are being overtaken by another vehicle. What should you do if an oncoming car appears close?
bank.explanation: If you are being overtaken and a car is coming towards you, you should drop back to create a larger gap for the overtaking vehicle to pull into safely.
options: Drop back to leave more room for the overtaking vehicle
Speed up so they can get behind you more quickly
Flash your lights at the oncoming vehicle
Move to the right to block the overtaking vehicle

bank.question: What should a driver do after missing the correct exit on a motorway?
bank.explanation: If you miss your exit, continue to the next one. Never reverse or attempt a U-turn on a motorway or slip road.
options: Reverse back along the hard shoulder
Perform a U-turn through the central reservation
Carry on to the next junction
Stop and wait for the police to help you

bank.question: When should you flash your headlights at other road users?
bank.explanation: Flashing your headlights should only be used to let other road users know that you are there. It should not be used to signal priority or show anger.
options: To alert other road users of your presence
To tell a driver they can pull out in front of you
To show that you are in a hurry
To thank another driver for giving way

bank.question: When driving and need to use a mobile phone, what should you do?
bank.explanation: A touch-tone phone (or any handheld device) is illegal to use while driving; you should find a safe place to stop before using it.
options: Find a safe place to stop before using it
Use it only when you are at traffic lights
Hold the phone with your shoulder while steering
Ask a passenger to hold the phone for you

bank.question: Which two types of road users are Toucan crossings specifically designed for?
bank.explanation: Toucan crossings are designed for both pedestrians and cyclists to cross at the same time. They are usually wider than Pelican or Puffin crossings.
options: Pedestrians and horse riders
Pedestrians and cyclists
Motorcyclists and cyclists
Disabled drivers only

bank.question: You are approaching a horse-drawn vehicle on a narrow road. What should you do?
bank.explanation: When a horse-drawn vehicle is approaching, you should stay well back and give them plenty of room, as horses are easily spooked.
options: Sound your horn to let them know you are there
Speed up to get past them as quickly as possible
Flash your headlights to show you have seen them
Give them plenty of room and stay well back

bank.question: You should keep your full-beam headlights on at all times when driving on unlit rural roads at night, regardless of oncoming traffic
bank.explanation: You must switch to dipped headlights when meeting oncoming traffic or following another vehicle to avoid dazzling other road users.

bank.question: You are turning right from a dual carriageway. What should you do if the central reservation is too narrow to contain your vehicle?
bank.explanation: When turning right from a dual carriageway with a narrow central reservation, wait until the road is clear in both directions to avoid obstructing other traffic.
options: Wait in the central reservation until the far side is clear
Proceed halfway and signal to oncoming traffic to stop
Turn quickly to avoid slowing down following traffic
Wait until the road is clear in both directions before turning

bank.question: Your vehicle is fitted with anti-lock brakes (ABS). How should you perform an emergency stop on a wet road?
bank.explanation: The safest way to stop on a wet or slippery road if your car has ABS is to press the brake pedal firmly and keep it pressed until you stop.
options: Pump the pedal rapidly to prevent locking
Apply the handbrake at the same time
Press the pedal firmly and keep it pressed
Release the pedal as soon as you feel it vibrate

bank.question: Coasting is a recommended technique to save fuel when driving down a steep hill
bank.explanation: Coasting (driving in neutral or with the clutch down) reduces your control over the vehicle, particularly braking and steering.

bank.question: When should you signal left when leaving a roundabout?
bank.explanation: When exiting a roundabout, you should signal left after you have passed the exit just before the one you intend to take.
options: After you have passed the exit before the one you want
As soon as you enter the roundabout
When you are halfway around the roundabout
The signal is not necessary if the road is clear

bank.question: You are at a level crossing with twin red flashing lights. What must you do if the lights continue to flash after a train has passed?
bank.explanation: Level crossings with a 'Keep Crossed' or 'St Andrew's Cross' sign and no barriers require extra caution; you should stay back until the lights stop flashing.
options: Speed up to get across before the train comes
Stay behind the stop line until the lights stop flashing
Drive across as soon as the train has passed by
Edges forward to see if another train is coming

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: This warning sign means roadworks are ahead. Slow down, look out for workers, cones, temporary lane layouts and possible speed restrictions.
bank.imageAlt: Triangular roadworks ahead warning sign
options: Mine ahead
Road closed ahead
Workforce exit
Road works ahead

bank.question: A triangular road sign with a red border and a picture of a car and a motorcycle means 'No motor vehicles'
bank.explanation: A triangular sign with a red border is a warning sign; a red circle with a car and motorcycle inside means 'No motor vehicles'.

bank.question: If your car does not have anti-lock brakes (ABS) and starts to skid during heavy braking, what should you do?
bank.explanation: If your car begins to skid and you don't have ABS, release the footbrake to allow the wheels to turn again and regain steering control.
options: Apply the handbrake firmly
Keep your foot hard on the brake pedal
Release the footbrake completely
Change into a lower gear immediately

bank.question: When joining a motorway from a slip road, you should?
bank.explanation: When joining a motorway, you should match your speed to the traffic already on the motorway to merge safely without causing a hazard.
options: Stop on the slip road and wait for a gap
Force your way into the left-hand lane
Drive slowly until someone lets you in
Adjust your speed to match the motorway traffic

bank.question: On a motorway, green reflective studs are used to mark the boundary between the slip road and the main carriageway
bank.explanation: Green reflective studs mark the edge of the main carriageway at slip road entrances and exits.

bank.question: When is it acceptable to overtake a vehicle on the left?
bank.explanation: Overtaking on the left (undertaking) should only be done if the vehicle in front is signalling to turn right or if traffic is moving in slow queues.
options: When you are in a hurry and the right lane is blocked
When you are on a motorway with three lanes
When the driver in front is driving too slowly
When the vehicle in front is signalling to turn right

bank.question: If your vehicle breaks down on a motorway, what is the best way to get help?
bank.explanation: The first thing you should do after a breakdown on a motorway is find the nearest emergency phone so the emergency services can locate you easily.
options: Use the emergency phone at the side of the road
Wait in your car for someone to stop and help
Attempt to repair the vehicle yourself to save time
Walk back along the motorway to the previous exit

bank.question: How should you apply the brakes in an emergency if your car has anti-lock brakes (ABS)?
bank.explanation: When your car has anti-lock brakes (ABS), you should apply firm, steady pressure to the brake pedal. Do not 'pump' the brakes, as this interferes with the system's operation.
options: Pump the brake pedal rapidly up and down
Press the brake pedal firmly and keep it pressed
Use the footbrake and handbrake together
Release the brake pedal if you feel it vibrating

bank.question: What does a Puffin crossing have that a Pelican crossing does not?
bank.explanation: At a puffin crossing, the sensors detect when pedestrians have finished crossing, meaning there is no flashing amber phase; it goes straight from red to steady amber then green.
options: A flashing amber phase
Sensors that detect if people are still crossing
A faster light sequence for cyclists
An audible signal that cannot be turned off

bank.question: You want to park but the only space available is for disabled badge holders. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Always look for an alternative parking spot. Do not park in a way that forces wheelchair users or parents with prams into the road.
options: Park on the pavement as long as you leave some space
Park with your hazard lights on to warn others
Park on the opposite side of the road facing traffic
Find a designated parking space or a legal roadside spot

bank.question: A steady amber light is used at a level crossing to warn you that the red flashing lights are about to start
bank.explanation: Traffic lights at level crossings (and some fire stations) use a steady amber light followed by twin flashing red lights to stop traffic.

bank.question: A circular blue sign with a red ring and a diagonal red line means 'No Entry'
bank.explanation: Blue circles generally give positive instructions (mandatory directions), such as 'turn left' or 'ahead only'.

bank.question: What does it mean if your ABS warning light stays on while you are driving?
bank.explanation: If the anti-lock braking system (ABS) warning light stays on while you are driving, it indicates a fault that needs to be checked by a professional immediately.
options: The handbrake is still on
The brake fluid is slightly low
The tyres are under-inflated
The ABS system is not working correctly

bank.question: You are turning right onto a dual carriageway. You should check that the central reservation?
bank.explanation: When turning right onto a dual carriageway, the central reservation must be deep enough to protect your entyre vehicle while you wait for a gap in the traffic.
options: Is wide enough to contain your whole vehicle
Has a 'Give Way' sign facing you
Is clear of all pedestrians
Has no trees or bushes blocking the view

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: A circular sign with a red border and a line through a bicycle indicates that cycling is not permitted in that specific area or path.
bank.imageAlt: A circular sign with a red border and a black silhouette of a bicycle with a red diagonal line through it
options: Route for cyclists only
Cyclists must give way to pedestrians
No cycling allowed
Parking for bicycles only

bank.question: You have just passed your driving test. What is a recommended way to build your confidence for motorway driving?
bank.explanation: Driving on a motorway for the first time can be intimidating. Taking a voluntary 'Pass Plus' course helps new drivers gain experience with motorways and night driving.
options: Take some lessons on motorway driving via Pass Plus
Drive only during the day for the first year
Wait until you have been driving for at least two years
Avoid the right-hand lane at all costs

bank.question: After driving through deep water, how should you dry your brakes?
bank.explanation: Deep water can cause brakes to become less effective. Drying them by light pressure while driving slowly is essential for safety.
options: Low speed and light pressure on the brake pedal
High speed and heavy pressure on the brake pedal
Normal speed and sharp pumping of the pedal
Drive in a low gear at high engine revs

bank.question: You are following a long lorry approaching a left-hand turn. Why might the driver move to the right?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles need more room to turn. As they turn left, they may first swing out to the right to clear the kerb.
options: The driver may swing out to the right before turning left
The driver will always stop before turning left
The lorry will speed up to clear the junction quickly
The driver will flash their headlights to signal they are turning

bank.question: How can you safely improve your vision when driving at night in built-up areas?
bank.explanation: At night, you should use your mirrors and your own observation to determine if it is safe. Using your horn is restricted in built-up areas except in emergencies.
options: Flash your headlights three times
Check your mirrors and signal long in advance
Slow down and look both ways at junctions
Sound your horn continuously

bank.question: You see a long lorry signalling to turn right, but it is positioned towards the left-side kerb. Why is this?
bank.explanation: Drivers of large vehicles often need to swing out to the left before turning right to clear the kerb with their rear wheels. Do not attempt to overtake them.
options: They are signalling in the wrong direction by mistake
They are planning to pull over and stop on the left
They have forgotten to turn off their indicator
They need to swing wide to clear the corner safely

bank.question: You are using a hands-free phone system while driving. What is the main danger?
bank.explanation: Using a mobile phone, even with a hands-free kit, significantly reduces your concentration and response times to hazards.
options: It is illegal regardless of the device used
It will improve your reaction times to hazards
It will seriously divert your attention from the road
It is only dangerous if you are driving on a motorway

bank.question: You are following a large lorry. Why should you stay well back?
bank.explanation: Large vehicles suffer from huge blind spots. If you cannot see their mirrors, the driver almost certainly cannot see you.
options: The driver cannot see you in their mirrors
The driver is about to turn left
The driver is slowing down
The vehicle is carrying a heavy load

bank.question: If your wheels lock during heavy braking in a car without ABS, you will lose the ability to steer the vehicle
bank.explanation: Braking too hard in a vehicle without ABS can cause the wheels to lock, which takes away your ability to steer the vehicle.

bank.question: Who is allowed to use a 'Toucan' crossing?
bank.explanation: Toucan crossings are designed for both pedestrians and cyclists to cross at the same time. Remember: 'Two-can' cross.
options: Motorcyclists and pedestrians
Pedestrians and cyclists
Trams and buses only
Horses and riders

bank.question: What do double yellow lines along the side of the road mean?
bank.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no waiting or parking at any time, unless signs specifically state otherwise.
options: No waiting at any time
No parking during daylight hours only
No stopping except to pick up passengers
No parking on weekends and bank holidays

bank.question: At what age does a car usually require its first MOT test?
bank.explanation: Standard MOT tests for cars are required annually once the vehicle reaches three years of age.
options: Three years old
Five years old
One year old tobacco
Seven years old

bank.question: What is a likely result of carrying a heavy load on a roof rack?
bank.explanation: Overloading your vehicle puts extra strain on the engine and increases aerodynamic drag, leading to higher fuel consumption.
options: Improved road holding
Increased fuel consumption
Lower insurance premiums
Better braking efficiency

bank.question: Which is the correct rule regarding motorway lanes?
bank.explanation: The right-hand lane of a three-lane motorway is for overtaking only; you should return to the left or middle lane once finished.
options: Keep to the left-hand lane unless you are overtaking
Stay in the right-hand lane to keep the traffic moving
Use the hard shoulder if the lanes are heavy with traffic
Only use the left-hand lane for slow lorries

bank.question: What information do signs with a blue circle give?
bank.explanation: Blue circles generally give mandatory instructions, such as 'turn left ahead' or indicating a route for specific vehicles like cycles.
options: Mandatory instructions or directions
Warnings of hazards ahead
Information about nearby facilities
Points of interest for tourists

bank.question: A 'cover note' is a document issued by an insurance company before they send out your actual insurance certificate
bank.explanation: A 'cover note' is the temporary document issued by an insurance company before the actual insurance certificate is posted or emailed.

bank.question: When should you adjust your speed when approaching a bend?
bank.explanation: Braking while cornering can cause the vehicle to lose stability or skid. It is best to brake to the correct speed before entering the bend.
options: Before you enter the bend
While you are turning the steering wheel
Just after the apex of the bend
Only if you feel the car sliding

bank.question: When driving on a narrow urban street and accidentally scrape the door of a legally parked car, what is the legal minimum insurance you must have to cover the damage to the other person's vehicle?
bank.explanation: Even if no one is injured, you are legally obligated to have at least third-party insurance to cover costs for any damage you cause to another person's property. This is the most basic level of cover permitted on UK roads.
options: Insurance that covers fire, theft, and accidental damage to your own car.
Fully comprehensive insurance.
Insurance that covers damage and injury to third parties.
Personal injury and legal expenses cover.

bank.question: What does a rectangular sign with a white background, a red horizontal bar, and a blue square indicate?
bank.explanation: If you see a sign indicating a dead end or 'No Through Road', you should not turn into it unless you need access to a property located there.
options: Cyclists only
One-way street ahead
No motor vehicles allowed
No through road for vehicles

bank.question: What is a likely cause of high-pitched wind noise while driving at speed?
bank.explanation: Excessive wind noise can be a sign that your doors are not closed properly or there is a gap in a window seal.
options: Door or window seals are damaged or open
The tyres are under-inflated
The engine oil is low
The brakes are worn out

bank.question: Where should you look to find the correct tyre pressure for your vehicle?
bank.explanation: Always check the vehicle handbook for the correct tyre pressure, as it may change depending on the load you are carrying.
options: The local petrol station attendant
The tyres themselves (embossed on the side)
The DVLA website
The vehicle handbook

bank.question: What does it mean if there are double white lines in the middle of the road and the line nearest to you is solid?
bank.explanation: Double white lines where the line nearest to you is solid mean you must not cross or straddle it, except in specific limited circumstances.
options: You can overtake if it is safe to do so
You must not cross or straddle the line
You may park your car on that side of the road
You are allowed to make a U-turn

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: A red circle with a car and motorcycle inside means that all motor vehicles are prohibited from entering.
bank.imageAlt: A circular sign with a red border containing a silhouette of a car and a motorcycle
options: No motor vehicles allowed
No cars or motorcycles on weekends
Only cars and motorcycles allowed
Route for emergency vehicles only

bank.question: You are following a cyclist on a narrow road. What should you do when you want to overtake?
bank.explanation: When following a cyclist, you must give them at least as much room as you would a car when overtaking, usually at least 1.5 metres.
options: Beep your horn to warn them you are there
Overtake as quickly as possible in the same lane
Follow closely so they know you want to pass
Give them as much room as you would a car

bank.question: Driving with under-inflated tyres can lead to increased fuel consumption
bank.explanation: Under-inflated tyres increase rolling resistance, which causes the engine to work harder and use more fuel.

bank.question: You are following a vehicle on a wet road. What time gap should you leave between your car and the vehicle ahead?
bank.explanation: When the road is wet, your tyres have less grip, increasing the distance it takes to stop; the gap should be doubled to four seconds.
options: Double the normal distance (four seconds)
Keep the same distance as in the dry
Triple the normal distance (six seconds)
Stay at least ten car lengths back regardless of speed

bank.question: You may park your car on a public road without road tax if you have declared it off-road via a SORN
bank.explanation: A 'Statutory Off-Road Notification' (SORN) only applies to vehicles kept off public roads; any vehicle parked or driven on a public road must be taxed.

bank.question: When driving in a built-up area at night with good street lighting, what lights should you use?
bank.explanation: At night, even if the road is well-lit, you must use dipped headlights so that you remain visible to other road users and pedestrians.
options: Side lights only
Dipped headlights
Full-beam headlights
No lights are required if there are streetlights

bank.question: Stopping distance in heavy rain is likely to be?
bank.explanation: In very heavy rain, stopping distances can be double those on dry roads due to reduced tyre grip.
options: The same as dry roads
Ten times the dry distance
At least double the dry distance
