Three times the dry distance

bank.question: You are navigating a tight city street with vehicles parked along the kerb. A police officer stops you and inspects your car, finding a deep cut on the sidewall of a tyre, exposing the internal cord. What is the legal implication of this defect?
bank.explanation: Any deep cut in a tyre that exposes the internal ply or cord is illegal, regardless of its location on the tyre. A vehicle with such a defect is considered unroadworthy and must not be driven.
options: You will be given a verbal warning and told to get it fixed.
The tyre is illegal and must be replaced immediately.
The tyre is only illegal if the cut is also on the tread face.
It is permissible to drive to a garage for a non-urgent repair.

bank.question: When must you stop your vehicle after being involved in an accident?
bank.explanation: You must remain at the scene, ensure the safety of others, and exchange details or report the accident to the police within 24 hours.
options: Only if someone is injured
Only if there is damage over £500
Only if you are at fault
In all cases where damage or injury is caused

bank.question: Over-inflating your tyres can reduce their grip on the road surface
bank.explanation: Over-inflated tyres have a smaller contact patch with the road, which reduces the amount of grip available.

bank.question: A circular traffic sign with a red border is used to give a warning of a hazard ahead, such as a sharp bend
bank.explanation: Circular signs with a red border are generally prohibitory signs, telling you what you must not do. Warning signs for hazards, such as bends, are normally triangular.

bank.question: What does this level-crossing sign mean?
bank.explanation: This sign warns of a level crossing without a gate or barrier. Approach carefully, look and listen for trains, and obey any lights or signs at the crossing.
bank.imageAlt: Warning sign for a level crossing without a gate or barrier
options: No through road for motor vehicles
Only cars and motorcycles allowed
Stop sign at a gated crossing
Level crossing without barrier

bank.question: What part of the car can be damaged if you use 'dry steering' (turning the wheels while the car is not moving)?
bank.explanation: Turning the steering wheel while the car is stationary (dry steering) can cause unnecessary wear to the tyres and steering mechanisms.
options: The gearbox and clutch
The tyres and steering rack
The engine oil and filter
The brake pads and discs

bank.question: You see a section of the road marked with white diagonal stripes and a broken white border. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Hatching with a broken border may be entered if it is necessary and you can see it is safe to do so.
options: Enter it only if it's necessary and you can see it's safe
Never enter it under any circumstances
Use it as a normal driving lane to overtake slow traffic
Park there if you need to use your phone

bank.question: How can you tell if the road you are driving on is icy?
bank.explanation: The first sign of the road becoming icy is often the steering feeling light or 'floaty', and the sound of the tyres on the road becoming very quiet.
options: The engine noise will increase significantly
The steering will feel light and unresponsive
The brakes will feel much firmer than usual
The windscreen will suddenly fog up with condensation

bank.question: What must you do when a pedestrian has stepped off the kerb onto a zebra crossing?
bank.explanation: You must stop and give way to pedestrians who have moved onto a zebra crossing. You should also watch out for people approaching the crossing.
options: Speed up to get past before they step out
Wave them across to show it is safe to cross
Stop and wait for them to cross
Sound your horn to warn them you are coming

bank.question: You are turning left into a side road. Why should you check for cyclists on your left?
bank.explanation: When a car is turning, the rear wheels take a shorter path than the front wheels. This makes the area near the side of the car dangerous for cyclists.
options: The cyclist will speed up to pass you
The cyclist will have to stop and wait
The cyclist will move to the right-hand side
The cyclist might be caught between your car and the kerb

bank.question: In icy conditions, your total stopping distance can be up to five times further than in dry weather
bank.explanation: Stopping distances can be up to ten times further in icy or snowy conditions due to the lack of tyre grip on the road surface.

bank.question: How much can your stopping distance increase when driving on icy roads?
bank.explanation: Stopping distances on icy roads can be up to ten times further than on dry roads. You should drive slowly in a high gear and leave a very large gap.
options: Two times further
Ten times further
Five times further
Twenty times further

bank.question: You see a vehicle with a flashing amber beacon. What does this usually mean?
bank.explanation: Vehicles with a maximum speed of 25mph, such as tractors, must use a flashing amber beacon when travelling on dual carriageways.
options: A doctor on an emergency call
A breakdown recovery vehicle only
A slow-moving vehicle on a dual carriageway
A police car in a pursuit

bank.question: You do not need to inform the DVLA if your health changes, as long as you feel competent to drive
bank.explanation: You must notify the DVLA if your health or eyesight deteriorates in a way that could affect your ability to drive safely.

bank.question: If you miss your intended motorway exit, what should you do?
bank.explanation: If you miss your exit, you must continue to the next one; reversing or turning back on a motorway is illegal and extremely dangerous.
options: Reverse back along the hard shoulder
Carry on to the next junction
Do a U-turn at the next gap in the reservation
Stop and ask for directions on the emergency phone

bank.question: Which type of road sign tells you what you must NOT do?
bank.explanation: Circular signs with a red border are generally prohibitive, telling you what you must not do. A red circle with a car and a motorcycle means no motor vehicles are allowed.
options: A red triangle
A red circle
A blue rectangle
A green square

bank.question: In which situation should you avoid overtaking?
bank.explanation: Overtaking is a high-risk manoeuvre. You should never overtake when your view of the road ahead is blocked, such as when approaching a dip or a hill.
options: When the speed limit is over 40 mph
When you are approaching a dip in the road
On a dual carriageway with three lanes
When the vehicle in front is moving slowly

bank.question: You see a ball bounce out into the road from between parked cars. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Always drive with anticipation. If you see a ball bounce into the road, assume a child might run out after it and slow down immediately.
options: Sound your horn and maintain your speed
Slow down and be prepared to stop
Speed up to get past the area quickly
Flash your headlights to warn others

bank.question: Directly following the car in front too closely is dangerous because?
bank.explanation: Tailgating (following too closely) is a common cause of accidents and can lead to road rage. You should always maintain a safe gap.
options: It is dangerous and can cause collisions
It reduces fuel consumption through drafting
It helps the traffic flow more smoothly
It is allowed if you are in a hurry

bank.question: How should you brake when driving on a road that is wet and slippery?
bank.explanation: Braking too hard on a slippery surface can cause the wheels to lock, leading to a skid. Brake gently and early.
options: Brake late and hard
Brake gently and early
Use the handbrake to slow down
Shift into a higher gear to slow down

bank.question: You're driving at night along a residential road lined with parked cars. Why should you avoid using full-beam headlights in this situation?
bank.explanation: In built-up residential areas, your full-beam headlights can easily shine into front-facing windows, disturbing residents. They can also cause significant glare for anyone sitting in a parked vehicle, either directly or through their mirrors.
options: The deep shadows created may obscure your view of the kerb.
The powerful glare makes it more difficult to judge your distance from the parked cars.
It is only legally permissible to use full-beam headlights on motorways.
The light can be reflected into the windows of houses or dazzle people within the parked vehicles.

bank.question: It is legal to use your hazard warning lights while driving to highlight your vehicle if you are running late for an appointment
bank.explanation: You should never use your hazard lights while moving to show you are in a hurry; they are for warning others your vehicle is obstructed or temporarily obstructing traffic.

bank.question: You see this sign at the entrance to a street. What does it mean?
bank.explanation: A red circle with a white horizontal bar is the standard sign for 'No Entry'. You must not drive past this sign into that street.
bank.imageAlt: A red circular sign with a thick white horizontal bar in the centre
options: No waiting during the day
One-way street ahead
Stop and wait for the green light
No entry for any vehicle

bank.question: When driving on a motorway in heavy rain, what should you use to help other drivers see you?
bank.explanation: Heavy rain creates a spray that significantly reduces visibility. Using dipped headlights helps you see and ensures other road users can see you.
options: Dipped headlights
Full-beam headlights
Rear fog lights only
Sidelights only

bank.question: You are turning into a side road and a pedestrian has already started to cross. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Pedestrians who have already started to cross a side road that you are turning into have priority according to the Highway Code.
options: Sound your horn and continue to turn
Wait and let them cross the road
Rev your engine to warn them to hurry up
Wave at them to show they should stop walking

bank.question: When are you allowed to stop on an urban clearway?
bank.explanation: Urban clearways are in place to keep traffic moving. You can stop only to set down or pick up passengers, but you must not park or wait there.
options: To load or unload goods for a business
To make a quick phone call in a safe place
To park for a maximum of 20 minutes with a permit
To pick up or set down passengers

bank.question: What do circular signs with a blue background generally do?
bank.explanation: Blue circular signs with a white border are used to give mandatory instructions, such as 'Turn Left' or 'Keep Left'.
options: Give instructions
Provide warnings of hazards ahead
Give information about distances
State speed limits

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: This prohibition sign means vehicles towing caravans are not allowed beyond the sign. It may be used where the road is unsuitable for towing, such as narrow, steep or winding routes.
bank.imageAlt: No towed caravans sign
options: Caravans ahead
No towed caravans
Caravan parking
Only caravans allowed

bank.question: What do red flashing lights above a motorway lane signify?
bank.explanation: Red flashing lights above a lane (an 'X') on a motorway mean the lane is closed and it is illegal and dangerous to drive in it.
options: The lane is only for emergency vehicles
You must not drive in that lane
You must speed up to get past the danger quickly
There is no speed limit in that lane

bank.question: In thick fog, you should use your full-beam headlights to see further through the mist
bank.explanation: Your high-beam headlights will reflect off the fog, creating a 'white wall' of glare that makes it harder for you to see the road.

bank.question: You should dip your headlights when following behind another vehicle to avoid dazzling the driver through their mirrors
bank.explanation: You should dip your lights when following or meeting other road users to avoid dazzling them, including pedestrians, cyclists, and horse riders.

bank.question: You see an elderly person waiting to cross the road. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Wait for the person to finish crossing; do not rev your engine or try to rush them, as this can be intimidating.
options: Be patient and allow them to finish crossing in their own time
Sound your horn to let them know you are waiting
Rev your engine to encourage them to walk faster
Drive around them if there is enough space

bank.question: While driving on a winding country road, where should you position your car for the best view before a sharp right-hand bend?
bank.explanation: By positioning yourself towards the left-hand side of your lane, you can see further around the right-hand bend and spot hazards earlier.
options: The right-hand side of your lane
The centre of the road
The left-hand side of your lane
The hard shoulder

bank.question: Why should you use a lower gear when driving down a long, steep hill?
bank.explanation: Engine braking uses the engine's compression to slow the car, preventing the brakes from overheating and failing on long descents.
options: To improve fuel economy
To increase the vehicle's speed
To prevent the brakes from overheating
To make the steering lighter

bank.question: When are you allowed to use the right-hand lane of a three-lane motorway?
bank.explanation: The right-hand lane of a three-lane motorway is strictly for overtaking. Once you have finished overtaking, you should move back to a lane on your left.
options: As an overtaking lane
When you are travelling at the speed limit
To allow other vehicles to join from the left
When you want to travel at a constant high speed

bank.question: The minimum legal tread depth for car tyres in the UK is 1.0mm
bank.explanation: The minimum legal tread depth for car tyres in the UK is 1.6mm across the central three-quarters of the breadth of the tyre.

bank.question: What can be caused by driving with a loose fuel filler cap?
bank.explanation: A loose filler cap can cause fuel to leak, which is a major skid hazard for motorcyclists and wasteful for the environment.
options: Improved fuel consumption
Increased engine power
Lower insurance premiums
Wasted fuel and a slip hazard for other road users

bank.question: What is the meaning of this road sign?
bank.explanation: This triangular warning sign means there is a roundabout ahead. Slow down, look for traffic from the right, and be ready to give way on approach.
bank.imageAlt: Triangular warning sign showing a roundabout ahead
options: Mini roundabout
3 way roundabout
Cycle roundabout
Roundabout approaching ahead

bank.question: What is meant by the term 'brake fade'?
bank.explanation: Brake fade is the loss of braking effectiveness caused by the brakes overheating, often due to heavy use on long downhill sections.
options: The brakes overheating from prolonged use
The brake fluid level being too low
Air getting into the hydraulic system
The brake pads being completely worn out

bank.question: On a motorway, the reflective road studs between the carriage and the central reservation are amber in colour
bank.explanation: Reflective studs on the right-hand edge of the motorway (next to the central reservation) are amber to help drivers navigate in low visibility.

bank.question: When driving at night on an unlit road, you should be able to stop within what distance?
bank.explanation: At night, you must ensure you can stop within the distance you can see to be clear with your own headlights.
options: The distance covered by your headlights
The distance you can see using your full beam lamps only
One car length for every 10 mph of speed
Twice the distance you would usually need in daylight

bank.question: You should avoid using a high-pressure hose to clean your engine bay as it can damage electrical components
bank.explanation: High-pressure cleaners can force water into electrical components or the air intake, potentially causing serious engine or electrical failure.

bank.question: Why should you give a cyclist extra room when you are overtaking them?
bank.explanation: Cyclists might wobble or swerve to avoid potholes or if they are buffeted by the wind. Always give them as much room as you would give a car.
options: They may swerve to avoid a drain cover or pothole
They are legally required to wobble to stay upright at low speeds
They are trying to get your attention to let you pass
They are signalling that they intend to turn right

bank.question: When may you enter a yellow box junction?
bank.explanation: Even if you have the right of way, you should not enter a yellow box junction unless your exit is clear. The exception is if you are turning right and waiting for a gap.
options: At all times when the traffic is heavy
Only when you are turning left
Only when your exit road is clear
When you are following an emergency vehicle

bank.question: What does a red cross displayed above a lane on a motorway mean?
bank.explanation: A red cross showing above a motorway lane means the lane is closed and you must not drive in it. This is often due to an accident or roadworks ahead.
options: There is an emergency phone ahead in that lane
You must not drive in that lane
The speed limit in that lane is 50 mph
You should speed up to clear the area quickly

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: This sign marks the end of a controlled parking zone. The zone-wide parking restrictions have ended, but you must still obey any local signs or road markings that follow.
bank.imageAlt: End of controlled parking zone sign
options: Stop and wait for the green light
Parking zone ends at times specified
Priority over parked vehicles
End of controlled parking zone

bank.question: If you are convicted of 'driving without due care and attention', the court can impose between 3 and 9 penalty points on your licence
bank.explanation: The three-point charge covers many offences including careless driving, which carries a fine and 3 to 9 penalty points.

bank.question: Which signal given by a police officer means "Stop"?
bank.explanation: A police officer or traffic warden will often stand with their hand up or out to signal traffic to stop. Red lights always mean stop.
options: An officer pointing towards a side road
An officer standing with an arm held up vertically
An officer waving you forward with a baton
An officer pointing at their own vehicle

bank.question: What might suggest that your engine oil has been contaminated by coolant?
bank.explanation: Oil mixed with coolant, often caused by a damaged head gasket, can leave a thick, creamy-coloured deposit under the oil filler cap.
options: A bright green liquid on the dipstick
Clear bubbles in the coolant tank
A thick, creamy-coloured deposit under the filler cap
Black soot around the exhaust pipe

bank.question: The legal minimum depth of tread for car tyres is 1.2mm
bank.explanation: The legal limit is 1.6mm across the central three-quarters of the breadth of the tread and around the entire outer circumference.

bank.question: You can legally drive a car on a public road without a valid MOT certificate for up to 14 days after it has expired
bank.explanation: A valid MOT certificate is a legal requirement to drive on public roads for most vehicles over three years old, and you cannot renew your road tax without one.

bank.question: If you are driving on a wet road, what might it mean if your steering suddenly feels very light?
bank.explanation: If your steering suddenly feels light, it is a classic sign of aquaplaning caused by water on the road surface separating the tyres from the tarmac.
options: The braking system is failing
The tyres are aquaplaning
The power steering fluid is low
The tyres are over-inflated

bank.question: What does it mean if you see red flashing lights above your lane on a motorway?
bank.explanation: Red flashes above your lane on a motorway mean that the lane is closed and you must move into a different lane as soon as it is safe.
options: A speed limit of 50 mph is in force
The lane is closed; you must not go any further in that lane
There is a service station ahead in that lane
A contraflow system is operating

bank.question: While driving down an urban street lined with parked cars when a ball bounces out into the road just ahead of you, how should you perform an emergency stop?
bank.explanation: In an emergency, you must act immediately to avoid the hazard. You should brake as firmly and as quickly as possible, while pressing the clutch to prevent the engine from stalling.
options: Swerve to the opposite side of the road while braking gently.
Brake firmly and quickly, depressing the clutch at the same time.
Apply the handbrake to bring the vehicle to a rapid stop.
Check your mirrors and then brake sharply.

bank.question: When should you reverse from a side road into a main road?
bank.explanation: You must never reverse from a side road into a main road because it is a dangerous manoeuvre that puts you and other road users at high risk.
options: Never
Only if the main road is clear of traffic
Only if you have a passenger to guide you
If there are no road markings at the junction

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: The blue sign with a white bicycle and a pedestrian indicates a route divided for cyclists and pedestrians to use simultaneously, but in their own lanes.
bank.imageAlt: A blue circular sign with a white bicycle and pedestrian separated by a vertical line
options: A route for pedestrians only
A route where pedestrians must yield to cyclists
A segregated route for pedestrians and cyclists
A prohibited zone for all vehicles except cycles

bank.question: Why should you stay well back when following a large vehicle?
bank.explanation: When following a large vehicle, you should stay well back. If you are too close, your view of the road ahead is restricted and the driver cannot see you.
options: So you can overtake more quickly if needed
To get a better view of the road ahead
To stop your engine from overheating
To allow other cars to pull in front of you

bank.question: Which types of vehicles are most vulnerable in strong winds?
bank.explanation: In very windy weather, high-sided vehicles like lorries are most likely to be blown off course or even tip over.
options: Motorcycles and mopeds only
Small cars with roof boxes
High-sided vehicles like lorries and buses
Tractors and slow-moving vehicles

bank.question: You are turning right from a dual carriageway into a side road. A pedestrian has already started to cross that side road. What should you do?
bank.explanation: When turning right from a major road into a minor road, you must give way to pedestrians who have started to cross the road you are turning into.
options: Sound your horn to warn them away
Flash your lights and continue turning
Wait and give way to the pedestrians
Speed up to get past before they cross

bank.question: Amber reflective studs on a motorway mark the boundary between the edge of the carriageway and the hard shoulder
bank.explanation: Amber reflective studs are found between the central reservation and the carriageway, not the hard shoulder. Red studs are used for the hard shoulder.

bank.question: Why would there be a height limit sign before a bridge?
bank.explanation: Bridges over a road may be lower than standard; drivers of tall vehicles must check their height against the displayed limit.
options: A narrow bridge ahead
The height of the bridge is limited
The bridge is weight-restricted
A swing bridge is ahead

bank.question: In relation to motor insurance, what is a 'cover note'?
bank.explanation: A cover note is the temporary document issued by an insurance company before the full insurance certificate arrives.
options: A temporary document issued before you receive your insurance certificate
A document that covers you for driving any car with permission
A notice sent by the police for a motoring offence
The document you receive when your MOT is due

bank.question: While driving through a tunnel, what is the recommended minimum time gap you should leave between you and the vehicle in front?
bank.explanation: To maintain a safe gap in tunnels, you should increase the following distance to at least 5 seconds.
options: 1 second
2 seconds
5 seconds
10 seconds

bank.question: In windy conditions, which of these road users are particularly vulnerable?
bank.explanation: In very windy weather, high-sided vehicles, motorcyclists, and cyclists are most at risk of being blown off course by sudden gusts.
options: Motorcyclists
Lorry drivers
Tractor drivers
Car drivers towing trailers

bank.question: Which gauge should you monitor closely when driving for long periods at high speeds on a motorway?
bank.explanation: Continuous high speeds can increase engine temperature. A quick glance at the temperature gauge helps ensure the engine isn't overheating.
options: The engine temperature gauge
The fuel gauge
The battery warning light
The oil pressure light

bank.question: Carrying a heavy load in your vehicle may require you to increase the air pressure in your tyres
bank.explanation: Heavy loads can affect the vehicle's centre of gravity and handling; you may need to increase your tyre pressure as per the manufacturer's handbook.

bank.question: What does a single yellow line along the side of the road mean?
bank.explanation: A single yellow line means parking is restricted during certain times. Always check the nearby signs for the specific hours of operation.
options: No parking at any time
No parking during daylight hours only
Waiting permitted for up to 30 minutes
Waiting restrictions apply at certain times

bank.question: When dealing with a zebra crossing, what is a correct safety rule?
bank.explanation: Stopping at a zebra crossing even when nobody is there is unnecessary and can be hazardous to vehicles behind you.
options: Stop at every zebra crossing even if no one is waiting
Speed up to get across the crossing before anyone steps out
Never wave a pedestrian across as there may be another vehicle coming
Park on the zigzag lines to go into a nearby shop

bank.question: What can cause 'brake fade'?
bank.explanation: Brake fade is the loss of braking power caused by the brakes overheating, often when used excessively on long downhill stretches.
options: The brake fluid level being too high
The tyres being worn down to the legal limit
Driving through deep water recently
The brakes overheating on a long journey downhill

bank.question: How much longer is the stopping distance on a wet road compared to a dry road?
bank.explanation: On a wet road, the stopping distance is at least double that of a dry road because there is less grip between the tyres and the surface.
options: The same as on a dry road
Two times less than on a dry road
At least double the distance on a dry road
Ten times the distance on a dry road

bank.question: How is a driver likely to be affected by drinking alcohol?
bank.explanation: A driver under the influence of alcohol may experience a false sense of confidence and take unnecessary risks.
options: Faster reaction times
Improved coordination
Better concentration on the road ahead
Increased confidence and risk-taking

bank.question: What is the purpose of the signs shown?
bank.explanation: Motorway countdown markers are blue rectangular signs with white horizontal stripes (or bars) that signal an upcoming exit, positioned 100 yards apart, beginning 300 yards before the start of the deceleration lane.
bank.imageAlt: Motorway countdown markers showing distance to the next exit
options: The central reservation line
Number of lanes on a motorway
Countdown marker to the next junction
The speed limit for the lane ahead

bank.question: You should wait to turn right at a dual carriageway if the central reservation is too narrow to contain your entire vehicle
bank.explanation: When the central reservation is narrow, an HGV or long vehicle may need to wait in the first half because its rear would overhang and block the other lane.

bank.question: In wet weather, you should increase the gap between your car and the vehicle in front to at least four seconds
bank.explanation: The two-second rule applies in dry conditions; in wet weather, you should at least double this gap to four seconds.

bank.question: You are being overtaken by another vehicle. What should you do?
bank.explanation: If you are being overtaken, you should maintain your speed so the overtaking driver can judge their manoeuvre safely. Slowing down might confuse them.
options: Speed up to get out of their way
Maintain a steady speed
Brake hard to let them pass quickly
Pull over to the hard shoulder immediately

bank.question: In wet weather, you should double the two-second gap between you and the vehicle in front to four seconds
bank.explanation: In dry conditions, you should maintain a two-second gap; in wet weather, this should be doubled to at least four seconds.

bank.question: What shape is a standard road sign that gives you a warning?
bank.explanation: Warning signs are almost always triangular with a red border to alert drivers to potential hazards ahead.
options: Circular with a blue background
Rectangular with a green background
Triangular with a red border
Octagonal with a red background

bank.question: In good daylight, what is the minimum distance from which you must be able to read a standard vehicle number plate?
bank.explanation: You must be able to read a standard vehicle number plate from a distance of 20 metres (approx. 66 feet) in good daylight. If you need glasses to do this, you must wear them whenever you drive.
options: 20 metres (66 feet)
12 metres (40 feet)
30 metres (100 feet)
5 metres (16 feet)

bank.question: What do yellow zig-zag lines on the road outside a school mean?
bank.explanation: Yellow zig-zag lines outside schools mean you must not park or stop, even to drop off passengers, to ensure children have a clear view.
options: Do not park or stop at all
Stop only to pick up children
Park only for a maximum of 10 minutes
Stop only if you stay with the vehicle

bank.question: What would suggest that your vehicle's suspension is worn?
bank.explanation: Bouncing after pushing down on the corners of a car suggests the shock absorbers are worn and need replacing.
options: Worn shock absorbers
Low tyre pressure
Loose wheel nuts
Brake failure

bank.question: What is a potential danger of overfilling your engine with oil?
bank.explanation: Overfilling your engine with oil can cause lead to leaks or internal engine damage due to increased pressure.
options: It will improve fuel consumption
It will make the engine run more quietly
It can cause oil leaks and damage the engine
It will help keep the engine cooler

bank.question: In wet weather, you should leave at least a four-second time gap between your car and the vehicle in front
bank.explanation: The two-second gap is for dry conditions; it should be doubled to four seconds in wet weather to allow for increased stopping distances.

bank.question: After driving through a town centre, you are now on a motorway. For which of these reasons may you stop on the hard shoulder?
bank.explanation: The hard shoulder on a motorway is for genuine emergencies only. You must not stop there to rest, make a phone call, or for other non-emergency reasons, but you must obey directions from a police officer.
options: To look at a map or check your sat-nav.
If you are instructed to do so by a police officer.
To answer a call on your mobile phone.
To have a short rest if you feel tired.

bank.question: When should you check your mirrors if you intend to change direction?
bank.explanation: You should check your mirrors before signalling to ensure your actions are safe and won't cause other road users to change speed or direction.
options: Wait until you have completed the turn
Signal first, then check your mirrors to see if anyone noticed
Check your mirrors before giving any signal
Flicker your indicator once before checking the blind spot

bank.question: Which type of road signs are used to give orders?
bank.explanation: Circular signs with red borders are almost always prohibitive, meaning they tell you something you must not do.
options: Red circles
Blue rectangles
Green squares
Yellow triangles

bank.question: While driving in fog, what is the maximum distance you should be able to see before you can legally use your fog lights?
bank.explanation: You should never use your front or rear fog lights unless visibility is seriously reduced to less than 100 metres (328 feet).
options: 100 metres (328 feet)
200 metres (656 feet)
300 metres (984 feet)
400 metres (1312 feet)

bank.question: If the rear of your car skids to the right while driving, you should steer quickly to the left to correct it
bank.explanation: To correct a rear-wheel skid, you should steer into the direction of the skid (the way the back of the car is sliding) rather than away from it.

bank.question: You are following a vehicle at night on a standard road. What should you do to avoid dazzling the driver ahead?
bank.explanation: Dipping your lights prevents the reflection of full beams from the mirror of the vehicle in front, which would dazzle the driver.
options: Switch to sidelights only
Switch on your hazard lights
Dip your headlights
Flash your headlights briefly

bank.question: Why is an Anti-lock Braking System useful in an emergency stop?
bank.explanation: ABS is designed to prevent the wheels from locking, allowing you to maintain steering control while braking firmly in an emergency.
options: It prevents your wheels from spinning on ice
It allows you to steer while braking harshly
It shortens your stopping distance in all conditions
It stops the vehicle automatically if a hazard is detected

bank.question: On an urban street, your dipped headlamp beam is correctly adjusted if the top of the beam shines below the windows of parked cars.
bank.explanation: Correctly adjusted dipped headlights should be aimed down and to the left. This prevents the beam from dazzling other road users, including drivers of oncoming vehicles and people in parked cars. An upward-pointing beam can be dangerous and may cause your vehicle to fail its MOT.

bank.question: Your driving licence will be revoked if you reach six or more penalty points within two years of passing your first practical test
bank.explanation: The New Driver Act states that if you reach 6 or more points within 2 years of passing your first test, your licence is revoked and you must reapply for a provisional licence.

bank.question: You are allowed to use your horn to alert a driver in front that they have not noticed a traffic light has turned green
bank.explanation: You should use your horn only to alert other road users of your presence or a potential danger, not to show annoyance.

bank.question: What does this sign mean?
bank.explanation: This sign means the route or lane is reserved for buses and cycles only. Other motor vehicles must not use it unless signs indicate an exception.
bank.imageAlt: Blue sign showing buses and cycles only
options: No buses or cycles at specified times
Priority over oncoming vehicles
Buses and cycles only
No route for buses and cycles

bank.question: Why are 'soft-top' cars considered to be at higher risk of theft?
bank.explanation: If your car has a soft-top or is a convertible, it is generally easier for someone to break in. Valuables should never be left inside.
options: They are faster and harder to catch
They are easier to break into than hard-top vehicles
They usually have more expensive sound systems
They have less effective alarms than other cars

bank.question: When driving through a well-lit tunnel, you are not required to use your headlights
bank.explanation: In a tunnel, you should use dipped headlights so that you remain visible to others and can see the road clearly, even if the tunnel is well-lit.

bank.question: Why is 'coasting' (driving in neutral for long distances) dangerous?
bank.explanation: Coasting (travelling in neutral or with the clutch down) reduces your control over the vehicle, particularly because there is no engine braking.
options: It improves fuel economy significantly
It makes the steering feel lighter
It reduces wear on the brakes
It reduces the driver's control over the vehicle

bank.question: When you are approaching a roundabout, you should normally give way to?
bank.explanation: While you should normally give way to vehicles already in the roundabout, you should also watch for those approaching and be prepared to stop.
options: Vehicles coming from the left
Vehicles coming from the right
Vehicles that are travelling fastest
Vehicles that have their indicators on

bank.question: You are waiting in a traffic queue at night. How can you avoid dazzling the driver behind you?
bank.explanation: When waiting in a queue of traffic at night, using the handbrake and releasing the footbrake prevents the dazzling effect of your brake lights on the driver behind.
options: Turn on your hazard warning lights
Keep your foot on the brake to show you are stopped
Switch off your headlights and use sidelights only
Use the handbrake and release the footbrake

bank.question: Driving with under-inflated tyres will help your vehicle achieve better fuel economy
bank.explanation: Under-inflated tyres increase rolling resistance, which makes the engine work harder and uses more fuel.

bank.question: The primary purpose of a catalytic converter is to reduce toxic gases and pollutants from the engine's exhaust
bank.explanation: Catalytic converters are part of the exhaust system and specifically reduce the amount of harmful pollutants, such as carbon monoxide, released into the atmosphere.

bank.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
bank.explanation: This sign indicates that the road ahead is a dead end or no through road for vehicular traffic.
bank.imageAlt: A blue square sign with a white 'T' shape. The top part of the T is red
options: A T-junction is ahead
No through road for vehicles
Hazardous dead-end for pedestrians only
A hospital is on the right-hand side

bank.question: What does a single red line at the side of the road mean on a 'red route'?
bank.explanation: Red routes are designed to keep busy traffic moving. Generally, you are not allowed to stop even to drop off passengers unless in a designated bay.
options: No parking but loading is allowed
No stopping at any time (unless signs state otherwise)
Speed limit is strictly 20 mph
Experimental traffic lane for electric vehicles

bank.question: When turning into or out of a side road, you should give way to pedestrians who are crossing or waiting to cross
bank.explanation: When turning into or out of a side road, you should give way to pedestrians who are crossing or waiting to cross that road. If they have started crossing, they have priority.

bank.question: What do solid white lines between lanes of traffic mean?
bank.explanation: Solid white lines are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, often to discourage lane changing near hazards.
options: The edge of the motorway
The start of a cycle lane
Traffic lanes moving in the same direction
A hazard warning line

bank.question: You are first on the scene of an accident involving an electric vehicle. What specific precaution should you take?
bank.explanation: A high-voltage battery can remain dangerous after a crash. You should only attempt to move the vehicle or touch its components if you are trained to do so.
options: Keep the air conditioning running to cool the battery
Douse the battery with water immediately
Open the battery vent caps to release pressure
Avoid touching any high-voltage cables or components

bank.question: On a motorway, green reflective road studs are used to mark the edge of the main carriageway at slip roads
bank.explanation: Green studs are used to indicate where slip roads or lay-bys leave or join the main carriageway.

bank.question: On a motorway, green reflective studs are used to mark the edge of the main carriageway at slip road entrances and exits
bank.explanation: Green studs mark the boundary of slip roads at junctions, helping drivers identify where the carriageway edge changes in the dark.

bank.question: A vehicle with a flashing amber beacon indicates that it is an emergency vehicle being driven by a doctor
bank.explanation: A vehicle with a flashing amber beacon is usually a slow-moving vehicle, such as a tractor or salt spreader, and is not an emergency vehicle.

bank.question: How can you prevent your wheels from spinning when driving on icy roads?
bank.explanation: Keeping your speed down and selecting the highest gear possible reduces the risk of wheelspin when driving on icy or slippery roads.
options: Use a high gear and low speed
Use a low gear and high speed
Use a low gear and low speed
Use a high gear and high speed

bank.question: Why should you take extra care when overtaking a motorcyclist on a windy day?
bank.explanation: In windy conditions, cyclists and motorcyclists can be blown off course by gusts, especially when passing open gaps or being overtaken by large vehicles.
options: Move closer to them to shield them from the wind
Stay directly behind them and flash your lights
Allow extra room when overtaking them
Overtake as quickly as possible to get past the danger

bank.question: Using a hands-free phone system while driving is safe because it does not affect your concentration
bank.explanation: While hands-free is legal, any use of a phone can be a significant distraction and may lead to a charge of driving without due care and attention.

bank.question: A catalytic converter is fitted to the exhaust system to improve the vehicle's fuel economy
bank.explanation: Catalytic converters reduce harmful exhaust gases like carbon monoxide, but they do not reduce fuel consumption; they can slightly increase it.

bank.question: Long white lines with short gaps in the centre of the road indicate a hazard is ahead
bank.explanation: The long white lines with short gaps are 'hazard warning lines', used when there is a hazard ahead such as a bend or a junction.

bank.question: Who must you notify if your health affects your ability to drive?
bank.explanation: You must notify the DVLA if your health or eyesight deteriorates in a way that could affect your ability to drive.
options: Your insurance company only
The DVLA
The local police station
The car dealership where you bought the vehicle

bank.question: What does a circular blue sign with a white arrow pointing to the bottom-left mean?
bank.explanation: Blue circles give mandatory instructions. This sign tells you to keep to the left of the obstacle or road furniture.
options: No entry for vehicles
Turn left ahead
Keep left
One-way street only

bank.question: Your car breaks down on a motorway and you manage to stop on the hard shoulder. Where is the best place to call for help?
bank.explanation: If you breakdown on a motorway, use the emergency telephone to contact the authorities, as they can pinpoint your exact location.
options: Call your insurance company on your mobile
Use the emergency telephone at the side of the road
Wait in your car for the motorway police to find you
Walk to the nearest exit and find a public phone box

bank.question: According to the Highway Code, where should you NOT park?
bank.explanation: Parking opposite a junction can obstruct the view of drivers pulling out and make it difficult for long vehicles to turn into the side road.
options: Opposite a bus stop
Opposite or within 10 metres of a junction
In a designated parking bay
In a one-way street

bank.question: What do flashing amber lights under a school warning sign mean?
bank.explanation: Amber lights on a school bus warn other road users that children may be getting on or off the vehicle.
options: The bus has broken down
The bus is speeding up
Children may be getting on or off the bus
The bus is about to turn right

bank.question: Who must you notify if your eyesight gets worse and does not meet the required standard?
bank.explanation: You must inform the DVLA if your eyesight deteriorates or if you develop a medical condition that could affect your driving safety.
options: The local police station
The DVLA
Your insurance company only
The Department for Transport

bank.question: Why is it dangerous to brake heavily as you enter a bend?
bank.explanation: Braking while cornering can cause the vehicle to lose grip and skid; it is safer to brake to the correct speed before entering the bend.
options: It improves steering control
It can cause the vehicle to skid or lose balance
It helps the suspension behave better
It ensures the tyres stay cooler

bank.question: What is a likely effect of carrying a very heavy load in your car?
bank.explanation: A heavy load can significantly change your vehicle's handling and increase your braking distance. Checking your tyre pressures is essential as they often need to be increased when carrying extra weight.
options: The vehicle's acceleration will improve
Your mirrors will provide a clearer view behind
The vehicle's handling and braking will be affected
The steering will feel much lighter than usual

bank.question: How will your stopping distance be affected if you are driving on a road with a loose surface?
bank.explanation: If you have to brake suddenly on a road with a loose surface, such as gravel, your stopping distance will be increased because of lower grip.
options: Remain the same as on tarmac
Decrease because the tyres 'dig in'
Be unaffected if you have ABS
Increase due to reduced grip between tyres and the surface

bank.question: You are moving off from behind a parked car. What should you do?
bank.explanation: When moving off from behind a parked car, you should check all mirrors and your blind spot to ensure it is safe for other road users.
options: Flash your headlights to warn others
Signal and pull out immediately while looking ahead
Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for a final check
Sound your horn to alert pedestrians on the pavement

bank.question: An advantage of a high-level third brake light is that it can be seen by drivers following several cars behind you
bank.explanation: High-set brake lights (at eye level) are effective because they can often be seen through the windows of the cars following immediately behind you.

bank.question: According to the Highway Code, you must use your headlights when visibility is reduced to less than how many metres?
bank.explanation: You must switch on your lights when visibility is seriously reduced, which usually means you cannot see more than 100 metres (328 feet).
options: 100 metres (328 feet)
200 metres (656 feet)
50 metres (164 feet)
The length of your vehicle

bank.question: In which situation should you use your hazard warning lights?
bank.explanation: If your car breaks down in a dangerous position, use your hazard warning lights to warn other road users of the obstruction.
options: When you are broken down and causing an obstruction
When you are parked on a clearway to pick up passengers
When you are driving at high speed in the fast lane
When you want to thank another driver for letting you out

bank.question: You see a pedestrian waiting to cross the road. They are carrying a white stick with a red band. What does this indicate?
bank.explanation: A person carrying a white stick with a red band is both deaf and blind. Take extra care as they may not see or hear your approach.
options: Deaf and blind
Just blind
Just deaf
Physically disabled

bank.question: If you are driving down an urban street with cars parked on one side. You notice a potential parking space, but the kerb is marked with double yellow lines, what does this indicate?
bank.explanation: Double yellow lines indicate that parking and waiting are prohibited at all times (24 hours a day, 7 days a week). Any exceptions, such as for loading or Blue Badge holders, will be specified on an accompanying sign.
options: Parking is for permit holders only.
No parking or waiting at any time.
Parking is not allowed on weekends.
You may stop for a maximum of 10 minutes.

bank.question: What does a continuous white line along the side of the road mean?
bank.explanation: A continuous white line on the side of the road marks the edge of the carriageway, helping drivers see the road boundaries in the dark or fog.
options: The edge of the left-hand side of the road
A hazard ahead requiring caution
No parking allowed at any time
A tram lane reservation

bank.question: What does a double red line at the side of the road indicate on a 'red route'?
bank.explanation: Red routes are used in some cities to maintain traffic flow; you are generally not permitted to stop at any time, even for picking up or dropping off passengers.
options: You can park for up to 10 minutes
You may not stop at any time on this route
Only buses and taxis are allowed to drive here
You can stop to unload heavy goods only

bank.question: If you are the registered keeper of a vehicle, you only need to update the DVLA about a change of address once per year
bank.explanation: As the registered keeper, you must tell the DVLA promptly if your address changes. You should not wait until a yearly update.

bank.question: What does it mean if a pedestrian is carrying a white cane with a red band?
bank.explanation: A person carrying a white cane with a red band is both deaf and blind. Take extra care as they cannot hear or see you.
options: The person is deaf
The person is physically disabled
The person is blind only
The person is deaf and blind

bank.question: While driving in heavy rain, what should you do if a vehicle is following you too closely?
bank.explanation: If a vehicle is following too closely behind you in heavy rain, increase your gap from the car in front to allow more room for braking.
options: Brake sharply to warn them to back off
Increase your following distance from the car in front
Switch on your hazard warning lights
Speed up to get away from them

bank.question: You are at a T-junction and your view to the sides is restricted by parked vehicles. What should you do?
bank.explanation: When emerging at a T-junction with parked cars obstructing your view, move forward slowly (creep) until you can see clearly.
options: Wait for a pedestrian to tell you it is clear
Move forward slowly until you can see past the cars
Sound your horn and pull out quickly
Move to the opposite side of the road to see better

bank.question: What can cause your steering to feel heavy?
bank.explanation: Under-inflated tyres can cause the steering to feel 'heavy' or difficult to turn because there is more friction with the road.
options: Under-inflated tyres
Over-inflated tyres
Worn brake pads
A loose fan belt

bank.question: Which lights should you use when driving through a well-lit tunnel?
bank.explanation: Dipped headlights are used in tunnels to help you see and be seen, regardless of how well-lit the tunnel appears to be.
options: Dipped headlights
Sidelights only
Full-beam headlights
No lights are required if the tunnel is well-lit

bank.question: You are checking your car's levels. What fluid should be kept between the 'Max' and 'Min' marks on the reservoir near the engine?
bank.explanation: In most modern cars, the fluid reservoir for the brakes is located in the engine bay and often has 'Max' and 'Min' markings.
options: The battery fluid level
The engine oil level
The brake fluid level
The coolant level

bank.question: How is the overall stopping distance of a vehicle calculated?
bank.explanation: The overall stopping distance is the sum of the thinking distance and the braking distance.
options: Braking distance plus following distance
Thinking distance plus braking distance
Thinking distance plus stopping distance
Reaction distance plus perception distance

bank.question: Which type of vehicle is most likely to be affected by side winds on an open, exposed road?
bank.explanation: High-sided vehicles, motorcyclists, and cyclists are particularly vulnerable to sudden gusts of wind when crossing high bridges or passing gaps in hedges.
options: Heavy lorries carrying gravel
Tractors and farming machinery
High-sided vehicles and motorcyclists
Compact electric cars

bank.question: What do hollow triangles or circles on a motorway gantry or sign indicate?
bank.explanation: Hollow triangles and circles are used on motorways to guide diverted traffic along a temporary route.
options: Emergency diversion routes for motorway traffic
Routes specifically for vehicles carrying dangerous goods
Recommended routes for heavy goods vehicles (HGVs)
The proximity of a Ministry of Defence site

bank.question: You are waiting to emerge from a junction and see a pedestrian waiting to cross the road you are turning into. What should you do?
bank.explanation: You should never wave a pedestrian across as there may be another vehicle approaching that you haven't seen. Wait for them to cross in their own time.
options: Wait patiently and do not wave them across
Sound your horn to tell them to cross
Wave your hand to show it is safe to cross
Flash your headlights to get their attention

bank.question: How does a puffin crossing differ from a pelican crossing?
bank.explanation: A puffin crossing uses sensors to track pedestrians; the red light for drivers stays on until the pedestrians have cleared the crossing.
options: A puffin crossing maintains the red light for drivers until the sensor detects the crossing is clear
A puffin crossing has a flashing amber stage for drivers
A puffin crossing is only for cyclists and pedestrians sharing space
A puffin crossing uses a steady green light for pedestrians at all times

bank.question: A pedestrian carrying a white cane with a red band indicates that they are visually impaired only
bank.explanation: If a person is carrying a white cane with a red band, it signifies that they are both deaf and blind.

bank.question: Why is it dangerous to leave your fuel filler cap loose after refuelling?
bank.explanation: A loose filler cap is dangerous because fuel can spill onto the road, creating a serious skid hazard for other road users, especially motorcyclists.
options: It will cause the engine to overheat immediately
It can spill fuel, creating a hazard for other road users
It will make your vehicle's alarm go off
It will significantly increase your car's top speed

bank.question: Why should you take extra care when driving near trams?
bank.explanation: Trams cannot steer to avoid you, and their tracks can be slippery, so you must give them plenty of room and never block their path.
options: Because they cannot steer to avoid you
Because they travel much faster than cars
Because they always have right of way at all junctions
Because they have noisy engines that can distract you

bank.question: When driving on a three-lane motorway, which lane should you use if the road ahead is clear?
bank.explanation: On a clear road at 70 mph, you should keep to the left-hand lane unless you are overtaking.
options: The middle lane
The left-hand lane
The right-hand lane
Any lane that is free of traffic

bank.question: When driving on a dual carriageway, which lane should you normally use?
bank.explanation: On a dual carriageway, you should usually stay in the left-hand lane unless you are overtaking or turning right.
options: Stay in the right-hand lane to allow others to merge
Stay in whatever lane you choose as long as you keep to the limit
Use the right-hand lane for through traffic only
Stay in the left-hand lane unless overtaking

bank.question: Why is it dangerous to use your brakes continuously while driving down a long, steep hill?
bank.explanation: Brakes can fade or overheat if used constantly on long descents. Using a lower gear provides engine braking to help control speed.
options: The brakes may overheat and become less effective
The engine will stall if you do not accelerate
The tyres will lose grip on the road surface
The steering will become heavy and difficult to turn

bank.question: Between what times must you NOT use your horn in a built-up area?
bank.explanation: You must not sound your horn between 11:30 pm and 7:00 am in a built-up area, unless a moving vehicle poses a danger.
options: From 10:00 pm to 6:00 am
From 11:00 pm to 6:00 am
From 12:00 am to 8:00 am
From 11:30 pm to 7:00 am

bank.question: How can you reduce the risk of becoming tired on a long journey?
bank.explanation: Planning your route before you set off helps you stay focused on the road rather than trying to find your way while driving.
options: Increase your speed to reach the destination faster
Drive in the middle of the road for a better view
Plan your route before starting the journey
Keep your hazard lights on at all times

bank.question: While driving on a motorway and see a vehicle with amber flashing lights stopped on the hard shoulder, what should you do?
bank.explanation: The 'Move Over' rule or general safety practice suggests you should move to an outer lane if safe to do so to provide a safety buffer for people on the hard shoulder.
options: Speed up to get past quickly
Stay in your lane and maintain speed
Flash your headlights to warn them
Move to another lane if it is safe to do so

bank.question: You are permitted to park on the zigzag lines at a pedestrian crossing if you are only stopping to pick up a passenger
bank.explanation: The zigzag lines are there to ensure pedestrians and drivers have a clear view. Parking there is illegal and dangerous.

bank.question: Why is it important to check your 'blind spots' before pulling away from the kerb?
bank.explanation: You must check your blind spots - areas that cannot be seen in the mirrors - before moving off or changing lanes to ensure there are no unseen road users.
options: To check if your indicators are working
To see if you are being followed by police
To check for vehicles in areas not visible in your mirrors
To make sure your door is shut properly

bank.question: Electronic Stability Control (ESC) is a system designed to help drivers maintain control of the vehicle during cornering or sudden manoeuvres
bank.explanation: Electronic Stability Control (ESC) is a computerised technology that improves a vehicle's stability by detecting and reducing loss of traction (skidding).

bank.question: If you are driving along an urban street and notice an ice cream van parked up ahead with its music playing, what is the main hazard you should be most aware of?
bank.explanation: An ice cream van is a strong indicator that children are nearby. They may be excited or distracted and cross the road unexpectedly without checking for traffic.
options: The van's music might make it difficult to hear emergency vehicle sirens.
Children, attracted by the van, might run into the road without looking.
The van might suddenly pull out without indicating.
The queue for the van may spill onto the road and block traffic.

bank.question: How much room should you give a cyclist when overtaking them?
bank.explanation: When overtaking a cyclist, you should give them at least as much room as you would give a car, as they may need to swerve to avoid hazards.
options: At least 50 centimetres (20 inches)
At least as much room as you would give a car
No more than a metre (3 feet)
Just enough to get past without touching them

bank.question: You are waiting to emerge from a junction and a car is approaching from the right. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Waiting until the car passes ensures you have a clear view and a safe gap; pulling out behind it could be dangerous if another vehicle is hidden.
options: Flash your lights at the car and pull out anyway
Speed up and pull out before the car reaches you
Wait for the car to pass before pulling out
Pull out immediately as people will slow down for you

bank.question: When driving on a well-lit motorway at night, which lights should you normally use?
bank.explanation: You must use dipped headlights at night on all roads, except where there is street lighting and a 30 mph limit, though even then they are often advisable.
options: Rear fog lights only
Full beam headlights at all times
Sidelights only
Dipped headlights

bank.question: You are parking facing downhill. How should you position your steering wheel for safety?
bank.explanation: To prevent the car from rolling into the road if the handbrake fails, turn the wheels towards the kerb so the tyre hits the kerb first.
options: Away from the kerb
Parallel to the kerb
Towards the kerb
In any direction as long as the handbrake is on

bank.question: Who must you inform if your health health condition deteriorates in a way that may affect your driving?
bank.explanation: You must notify the DVLA of any medical condition that could affect your ability to drive safely, such as certain heart conditions or epilepsy.
options: Your local police station
Your insurance company only
The DVLA
Your GP only

bank.question: How can you help to keep your car as environmentally friendly as possible?
bank.explanation: Over-revving the engine or harsh acceleration wastes fuel and increases emissions, whereas staying in a higher gear helps efficiency.
options: Drive in lower gears at all times
Accelerate quickly until the speed reaches the limit
Avoid over-revving the engine in lower gears
Use the handbrake to slow down instead of the footbrake

bank.question: Which vehicle must display a flashing amber beacon when travelling on a dual carriageway?
bank.explanation: Vehicles with a top speed of 25 mph or less, such as tractors or certain road works vehicles, must display an amber flashing beacon on dual carriageways.
options: A vehicle limited to 25 mph
An ambulance on an emergency call
A security van transporting cash
A doctor on a private call-out

bank.question: Most circular traffic signs with a red border are used to give orders that are 'prohibitory'
bank.explanation: Circular signs with red borders are almost always prohibitive, telling you what you must not do.

bank.question: If you are driving on a road with parked vehicles on your side, what should you do if an oncoming vehicle is approaching?
bank.explanation: Even if you have the right of way, if an oncoming vehicle is already in the gap, you should slow down or stop to let them through to avoid a gridlock.
options: Speed up to get through first
Flash your headlights to claim priority
Sound your horn and keep moving
Give way to the oncoming vehicle if they have already entered the narrow section

bank.question: Why might a long vehicle swing out to the left before turning right at a junction?
bank.explanation: Longer vehicles, such as lorries and buses, may need to swing out to the left before turning right to clear the kerb.
options: They are signalling incorrectly
The vehicle needs more room to turn right due to its length
The driver is planning to pull over on the left first
They are trying to overtake a cyclist on the right

bank.question: You are parked on an urban street and preparing to set off on a long journey. To get an accurate reading, when is the correct time to check your tyre pressure?
bank.explanation: For an accurate reading, you should always test your tyre pressures when the tyres are cold. Driving causes the tyres to warm up, increasing the pressure of the air inside and leading to a misleadingly high reading.
options: Only when the tyre pressure warning light on the dashboard comes on.
After driving for at least 20 minutes to warm the tyres.
At a service station midway through your journey.
Before starting your journey, while the tyres are cold.

bank.question: How can you drive in a way that helps the environment?
bank.explanation: To help the environment and save fuel, you should look well ahead to avoid unnecessary braking and acceleration, which maintains a steady speed.
options: Drive in a lower gear at all times
Look ahead and avoid unnecessary acceleration or braking
Keep the engine revving while stationary to prevent stalling
Use the air conditioning on its maximum setting

bank.question: When may you use your hazard warning lights while driving?
bank.explanation: Hazard warning lights are used to warn other road users of a breakdown or an obstruction ahead, but you must not use them as an excuse for illegal parking.
options: When you are double-parked on a busy street
When you are driving in very heavy rain during the day
To thank a driver who has let you out of a junction
When your vehicle has broken down and is causing an obstruction

bank.question: When driving in a city centre and see a tram, what should you do?
bank.explanation: Trams cannot steer to avoid you and they are very quiet, so you must always give them priority.
options: Wait for them to signal you through
Flash your lights to show you are there
Give way to them, as they cannot steer to avoid you
Sound your horn to warn them of your presence

bank.question: When driving on a motorway in heavy rain and your car begins to aquaplane, what should you do?
bank.explanation: If your car begins to aquaplane (slide on a layer of water), you should stay calm and ease off the accelerator to regain grip.
options: Ease off the accelerator and do not brake hard
Brake firmly and steer towards the side of the road
Turn the steering wheel rapidly from side to side
Shift into a lower gear and accelerate out of it

bank.question: An elderly person is slowly crossing the road in front of you. What should you do?
bank.explanation: Wait for the person to finish crossing. Do not wave them across, rev your engine, or move forward until the crossing is clear.
options: Wave them across to show it is safe
Rev your engine to encourage them to hurry
Be patient and wait for them to finish crossing
Drive behind them while they are still on the crossing

bank.question: A continuous white line along the edge of the road means that you are not allowed to park there at any time
bank.explanation: A continuous white line down the side of the road marks the edge of the carriageway; parking is permitted unless there are specific yellow line restrictions.

bank.question: You've registered your car with a Statutory Off Road Notification (SORN). What is the trigger for the SORN to be cancelled?
bank.explanation: A SORN stays in place until you tax the vehicle again, sell it, or have it scrapped. It no longer needs to be renewed each year.
options: If the vehicle is given a new MOT certificate.
When the vehicle is taxed again.
After a period of 12 months has elapsed.
When the current insurance policy expires.

bank.question: When driving in a city with trams, you should be extra cautious because trams cannot steer to avoid you and move silently
bank.explanation: Trams are powered by electricity and run on fixed rails, making them very quiet and unable to steer out of your way.

bank.question: It is always legal to overtake a slower vehicle on the left on a three-lane motorway if the right-hand lanes are congested
bank.explanation: Overtaking on the left is only permitted in specific circumstances, such as in slow-moving queues or when the vehicle in front is signalling to turn right.
